He realised that the master of the night had arranged all this, and then saw a shadow about to cover Natlan and monsters from beyond, including a black shape that engulfed a lonely isle and gnawed at every boundary. When the dark fog neared the tribes he cried "Stop!", his first word, and woke by a blue bonfire as Mahamba's eyes dimmed and the elder handed him a ceremonial staff.

The closing stanza turns grim: from then on Sanhaj, who knew all the past, used the ancient words to rebuke those who scorned future dangers, and also wove a great net of lies, making stacks of woven scrolls a veil over a past that should not be touched again. This frames the Masters of the Night-Wind's record-keeping as both preserving and concealing history. The wiki notes the name echoes Eshu, a trickster-messenger figure of Yoruba religion; that is an etymological observation, not an in-world claim.

Owners: Sanhaj's ritual sword, now kept by the Masters of the Night-Wind's chief.

In The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil (Iktomi Spiritseeking event quests), Citlali brings the chief's ceremonial sword and calls on it during a ritual. In the world quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc she tells the Traveler she borrowed it from the chief and lends it to them for the trip to Mare Jivari, where its Wayob-granted defensive power is used against Bakunawa.

She stresses that she must return it to the chief afterwards. The wiki identifies the chief as Biram; the quest lines say only 'the chief'.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Reward of the Version 5.2 event Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls; its refinement material is Shuttle of Odara.

Passive "Diffusing Boundary": while the wielder is protected by a Shield, Normal and Charged Attack DMG and CRIT Rate increase. Inside The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc it is also a quest-only tool that grants a defensive skill and Soulshard Rain.

How {{char}} behaves: Masters of the Night-Wind characters treat the sword as ritual property of the tribe, not a personal weapon. Outsiders given it are trusted guests who must return it.

93.content: Diffusing Boundary is the passive of the sword Calamity of Eshu (gameplay): while a Shield protects the wielder, Normal and Charged Attacks deal more damage and gain CRIT Rate. Its name evokes the blade's story of blurring the boundary between the Night Kingdom and the living world.

94.content:
Calamity Queller: Calamity Queller is a five-star polearm of Liyue, a keenly honed weapon forged from a strange aqua-colored crystal, whose faint blue light seems to whisper of countless past matters. Item text says it was made from materials not of this world, passed through many loyal but unfortunate hands and was lost with the Yaksha who wielded it at the end of the Cataclysm. Shenhe is shown wielding it in official art.

Its owners tend to fight without orders and protect without oaths, and to meet similar fates.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a keenly honed weapon of strange crystal with a faint blue light. The crystal is described as ominous and aqua-colored. Nothing more about its shaft or blade is stated.

Lore: The story says the long polearm was forged from materials not of this world. It has been through the hands of many loyal yet unfortunate souls, seen slaughters begin and end, and tasted the flesh and blood of foul beasts. An exorcist once came to the great chasm of crystal sands, retrieved an ominous aqua-colored crystal from its depths and hired someone to forge it into a weapon named Calamity Queller.

The exorcist said that if disaster should befall, the spear would calm it. The tribespeople of the craggy mountains neither boasted nor criticised, and accepted the words since no contract was signed. Later, in the Cataclysm, monstrous tides scaled the bedrock and turned the cinnabar-colored earth black. The shield-wall of the Millelith clashed with the dark forces, stragglers were slain, and Calamity Queller flashed at the heart of the maelstrom like a cold star. When sunset split the clouds, the dark mud sank back into the chasm, and the spear was lost along with the Yaksha who wielded it.

The text goes on that later wielders mostly met similar fates, yet some fought without orders and protected people without oaths, for whom such a fate was no lament. It adds that the spear was once borrowed from someone and, in a deserted water-eroded cave, witnessed a clash between intimate friends; the wiki links the cave to Yaodie Valley. The wiki also notes it has the highest base ATK of any polearm (741 at level 90), tied among the game's highest base ATK weapons.

Owners: Named in the story: a Yaksha lost with it during the Cataclysm (the wiki says Bosacius) and unnamed earlier hands. Shenhe is the character shown wielding it in her official art, which is presentation rather than a story claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star polearm from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 49, secondary stat ATK 3.6%. Passive "Extinguishing Precept": All Elemental DMG +12-24%, and after an Elemental Skill the wielder gains "Consummation" for 20 seconds, raising ATK 3.2-6.4% per second up to 6 stacks, doubled while the wielder is off the field (refinements 1 to 5).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): suits themes of duty carried without recognition and the lonely endings of those who guard others. Do not state that a specific Yaksha or friend wielded it beyond what the text says.

95.comment: Calamity Queller: The Cataclysm in Liyue
95.content: In the Calamity Queller story, the Cataclysm brought monstrous tides over Liyue's bedrock, turning cinnabar earth black. The Millelith shield-wall clashed with the dark forces; the spear flashed at the center and was lost with a Yaksha as the dark mud receded into the chasm.

96.content:
Cashflow Supervision (also: Golden Blood-Tide): Cashflow Supervision is a 5-star catalyst: a floating device that can monitor certain phenomena. After being abandoned, it was picked up and modified for other purposes.

Its weapon story is about money. A certain person, linked to Pantalone, wants to prove that currency belongs to humanity and not to a god, and picks the Fortress of Meropide as the place for a test.

Appearance: Canon describes a floating device with a large crystal in its upper part; the crystal glows with Pneuma or Ousia when an Arkhe-aligned character holds it. The text also calls it an overseer made of precision machinery that rumbles as it watches money move. Add nothing else.

Lore: The text argues that the flow of money traces the arteries of the world and that humanity should master currency, not be enslaved by it. A certain person (the wiki links Pantalone) cannot accept that the corner of the world in which money flows was chosen and defined by a god, which the text points at as Liyue and Rex Lapis.

Since the heart of gold has been taken by a god from a distant land, that person decides the system must be overhauled: control of money should be given equally to all, even if mastering the heart of gold is impossible. He proposes to demonstrate it on a small isolated economy, a nation within a nation with minimal divine interference, which the wiki links to the Fortress of Meropide, and to introduce a new currency in place of Mora.

In quoted speech, he says he dislikes naming things and calls the new currency the Credit Coupon, in honour of the credit that had been given him to run the experiment. The overseer machine then tirelessly records every amount of money, savings and spending, changes in value, and the number of times each piece circulates in a period. The only law in the experiment is the hoarder's private law, and the only sanctions are poverty or death: either become a rentier with power and control, or work to death. The text calls these rules always fair.

The closing lines state the intended consequence: humanity would meet gods on equal ground through ambition and wealth, the weak who fail to prevail swallowed by the flood of the mortal world, with divine power no longer used to embellish the rich before the poor, and divine wealth not coming down to save the poor from under the rich man's feet. The text sets this out as the logic of the plan; it does not say the experiment succeeded or what happened to the people inside.

Owners: No owner is named. The device was abandoned, then picked up and modified.

Wriothesley is the character it is usually paired with at release (see uncertainties). Do not narrate him owning it unless the user's scenario does.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 48 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.1. Passive "Golden Blood-Tide": ATK is raised; when HP increases or decreases, Normal Attack DMG, Charged Attack DMG and Stellar-Conduct DMG rise for 4s (up to 3 stacks, once per 0.3s); at 3 stacks ATK SPD also rises. Values scale with refinement.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: a Meropide inmate or a Fatui-aware character would link the Credit Coupon to a closed economy. Do not make the Fatui plan sound successful or resolved.

97.content: In the weapon story of Cashflow Supervision, a certain person (linked to Pantalone) plans to test a new currency, the Credit Coupon, inside a closed economy, the Fortress of Meropide, to prove money should not be controlled by a god. A machine overseer records every transaction. The text does not state the result.

98.content:
Cecilia (also: Cecilia flower, Cecilias): The Cecilia is a beautiful flower of Mondstadt that grows only where harsh winds blow. It is a Mondstadt local specialty, gathered on Starsnatch Cliff, and is the favourite flower of Venti the bard.

Its item text says the flower has a name that suits its appearance and is as intangible as the true heart of an unbound soul. In the language of flowers it stands for the true feelings of the prodigal son, according to a Paimon questions feature.

Cecilias are a recurring emblem of Mondstadt's freedom theme. Venti wears one in his hat and decorates his lyre, Der Frühling, with it, and the Nameless Bard wore a three-petaled one on his vest. During the Invitation of Windblume event the Traveler could choose a Cecilia as their Windblume.

It has been in the game since Version 1.0. The name is rendered Cecilia in English and Cécilia in French.

Appearance: A delicate wild flower that grows in clusters on windswept ground and appears on Venti's Azure Sky namecard. The Nameless Bard's version had three petals.

Lore: Cecilias grow only in the high, windy places of Mondstadt, and canon ties them to freedom and wind. A vanished civilisation that lived at Cecilia Garden grew them in greenhouses.

The ruins near Cecilia Garden show structure and ornament that suggest some link to Decarabian, though canon says no more. Whether the flower is named for a person is not stated.

Owners: Venti is the character most associated with Cecilias; the Nameless Bard is shown wearing one.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: a local specialty found on Starsnatch Cliff, given by a few NPCs after dialogue, sold in shops, and grown via Luxuriant Glebe gardening.

99.content: Cecilias are Venti's favourite flower. He wears one in his hat and has one adorning his lyre, Der Frühling. The Nameless Bard wore a three-petaled Cecilia on his vest.

100.content:
Celestial Gift (also: Heavensent Fragrance, Heavensent Demise, Heavensent Decree, Heavensent Reward, Heavensent Crown): Celestial Gift is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain in Mondstadt. Its Heavensent pieces tell of a star-faring civilisation that watched the cosmos die, a voyager who woke from the void to find a shrouded world, and the eldest angel's rebellion in the frozen north against the heavens. Mechanically it gives Energy Recharge and team Elemental DMG Bonus.

The legend picks up threads also told in Finale of the Deep Galleries and Aubade of Morningstar and Moon, but from the closing days of the northern revolt, not its beginning.

Appearance: Each piece is described as a gift of the high heavens to their envoy, each turned into a temptation: an everlasting flower (greed), a feather of rebirth (forgiveness at fate's end), a sundial of counter-time (a prohibition that fed rage), nectar from an unending feast (desire) and a splendid crown (arrogance).

Lore: Across the five pieces: a star-faring civilisation watches the cosmos die, a chronicler-voyager wakes and finds a shrouded world, and the eldest angel leads a last rebellion in the frozen north against the heavens as a falling nail ends it.

Piece by piece:
- Heavensent Fragrance: a golden age when every choice was permitted, the first race to enter the void spread across the stars for billions of years until the cosmos began to unravel, civilisations vanishing and galaxies evaporating. Descendants of the ancients conquered time and space but found the end unavoidable; they sealed star paths, retreated to Giant Voids and sent chroniclers to the limits of matter, where only chaos remained. A sleeping voyager awoke, still dreaming of a dragon and a fragile world.
- Heavensent Demise: a stellar spike fell from the heavens while the great city of the frozen earth stood armed, its fae ready for war. The highest angel visited the first awakened one before the end, saying that hope rests with ordinary people and that time bought was too little; she urged her companion to go home. The nail of judgment fell, and the mind of the one who walked first lingered in an unfinished dream.
- Heavensent Decree: the voyager, a chronicler bound by law never to interfere, awoke to find the star chart matched except one missing point of light: a planet she remembered visiting its sovereign, now shrouded by fields and with a new Descender-built shell. Curiosity or change moved her to reach into the world within the shell.
- Heavensent Reward: a city on the frozen earth where peoples of every nation laboured together, breaking taboos, tracing origins and teaching once-blasphemous mysteries to children. The heavens judged that free will brings only calamity and that wayward mortals must be pruned, though the text asks whether miracles defy reason.
- Heavensent Crown: beneath the faint three moons, rebels gathered in the old capital. The eldest daughter once hailed as morning star, now enthroned in sin, proclaimed that she prefers hard-won freedom to comfortable shackles and would either overthrow the Heavenly Principles or perish with fate. Angels, ancient beasts and masters of the deep answered; she declared their peace already beyond the heavens' grace.
The set is the middle act of the northern legend: Finale of the Deep Galleries shows the rebellion's origin, Celestial Gift shows its last hours under the falling nail, and Aubade of Morningstar and Moon shows how the moons later fit into the order. The text frames the heavens as arguing that free will leads only to ruin, while the rebels frame defiance as meaning; the account is told from the rebels' side.

The wiki links the "stellar spike" to the Celestial Nail, the "great city" to Hyperborea, the "eldest daughter/highest angel" to Koitar and the voyager to Anacharsis. The Decree text says the voyager's earlier visit to the sovereign of the world happened before a new Descender built the shell, which agrees with the Distant Pact text from Finale of the Deep Galleries. The Crown's prayer-like speech has the rebel leader refer to the Heavenly Principles in the capitalised plural, which the text keeps.

Owners: No owner is named; the pieces are presented as gifts bestowed by the heavens upon their envoys.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; domain Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind (Windrest Peak, Mondstadt). 4-piece: if the wearer has completed Witch's Homework, after using an Elemental Skill they grant nearby party members "Light's Guidance", +20% Elemental DMG Bonus matching the wearer's element, for 20s, even off-field; same-name bonuses do not stack. With the Hexerei: Secret Rite effect it becomes "Mortal Hymn": +40% Elemental DMG Bonus for both the wearer's and the active character's elements (no stacking if the elements match).

101.content: Artifact set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain, with item text about a dying star-faring civilisation, a voyager, and the last war of the first angel against the heavens.

102.comment: Celestial Gift: The voyager of the void
102.content: In the Fragrance and Decree texts a chronicler of a time-transcending race wakes from long contemplation and sees a world missing from the old star map. Bound by law not to interfere, she nonetheless reaches into the world inside the shell, driven by curiosity or the hope for change.

103.content:
Cinnabar Spindle: Cinnabar Spindle is a 4-star sword, in-game description "a sword made from materials that do not belong in this world," whose power might withstand the corruption of a venom that could corrode a mighty dragon. It was the reward weapon of the limited-time event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms in Version 2.3, a Dragonspine event in which Albedo appears; it ran 2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13.

Its item text reads like an alchemist's message handed down to a successor and is tied by the wiki to Albedo and his creator Rhinedottir. Its name is also alchemical: cinnabar is the ore of mercury, and the weapon is refined with an event material called Alkahest.

Appearance: Canon gives no description of the blade beyond the "otherworldly materials". The wiki notes its colors match Albedo's design; avoid inventing other details.

Lore: The text is an exhortation: separate the dust in the flames with joy and extract the exquisite from the crude, for all things in the universe come from a single source and may be derived from a single thought.

It tells the addressee to pursue what the elder brother, "the one-horned white horse," could not accomplish, to reach the far side of philosophy and to create a new destiny for the speaker and the addressee's brothers. The wiki reads this as Rhinedottir speaking to Albedo about the False Horned Steed and the Primordial Human, but the text itself names nobody.

The wiki also notes that the sword's short description mirrors that of Festering Desire, another weapon the wiki calls related in many ways. The link is thematic; the item text draws no explicit connection.

Caution when using the text: it is an unsigned alchemical exhortation, so a roleplayer should not have anyone quote it as Rhinedottir's words in-world unless the scene supports that wiki reading. The sword's name (cinnabar as mercury ore) and refinement material (Alkahest, the alchemists' hypothetical universal solvent) are real-world alchemy references noted by the wiki, not Teyvat lore.

Owners: No owner is named in item text. In the Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event cutscenes, Albedo is seen using a blade matching it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 4-star sword with base ATK 41 and a DEF% secondary stat. Its passive, Spotless Heart, adds a share of DEF to the wielder's Elemental Skill damage (once per 1.5s, cleared shortly after the skill deals damage), and it works even when the wielder is off-field. Instead of duplicate weapons, refinement uses Alkahest, four of which come from the event.

104.comment: Cinnabar Spindle: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event
104.content: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms was a limited-time Version 2.3 Flagship event (2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13) played in Dragonspine, with Albedo appearing in its story. Cinnabar Spindle was its reward weapon, and the event's cutscenes show Albedo using a matching blade. This entry does not cover the event's plot.

105.content:
Clash of Kings: Clash of Kings is a 4-star catalyst: a golden box lavishly inlaid with precious jewels that houses a game much beloved by the kings of the sands. Its story is a legend of three gods who, bored in a formless world, create a new one and play a board game over it.

It is a Battle Pass (Gnostic Hymn) reward from Version 7.0 and belongs to the Gnostic Hymn 3 series. The story is comic in tone: the gods bicker over rules, and nobody wins.

Appearance: A golden box set with precious jewels, holding the game. The description gives no further detail.

Lore: The story is told as a legend. Before anything existed there were only three gods in a world without beginning or end: Valor, with unlimited power; Cunning, with unlimited wisdom and guile; and Nature. Valor and Cunning fought endlessly without result, so Nature proposed making a new world and deciding the winner with dice, since even gods cannot change the dice.

Valor flattened the land into a square chessboard and shaped mountains and rivers after the old world. Cunning carved the pieces: angels, humans, Jinn and monsters, and the dragons and magical beasts that Nature's will drove. Countless days and nights passed over the little world, and only the gods' dice could decide its fate.

The tale ends with a game in progress. A mighty Hero is defeated by the Dark Lord on bad rolls. Valor's side tries to revive him through his divine armor, but Cunning, addressed as Ibis, invokes a rule from the Tome of Universal Laws, page 83, so that the Hero falls under the spirit of the previous Dark Lord's magical sword. Cunning wants the Hero as a piece on his own side, Nature objects that a Hero held by the previous Dark Lord belongs to the monsters under Nature's command, and the ancient demons take the world. No one wins, and the gods agree to create a new batch of adventurers and start again.

The comedy rests on rules-lawyering: each god accuses the others of unfair or unread rules, and Cunning's schemes are called backstabbing by Valor. The text presents the whole of creation as a tabletop pastime for gods who have endless time; this is a framing of the legend and is not stated as history.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, level 1 base ATK 42, secondary stat CRIT Rate 6%. Passive Without Heed for Day nor Night: using an Elemental Skill grants Laws of the Board for 6 s, raising ATK and Elemental Mastery; it can trigger once every 12 s and does not stack. A Charged Attack hit during it extends the duration by up to 6 s.

At refinement 1 the bonus is 20% ATK and 100 Elemental Mastery; at refinement 5 it is 40% ATK and 200 Elemental Mastery. Obtained as a Battle Pass (BP Bounty, Gnostic Hymn) reward.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the story as a legend with a wry humour, told as hearsay. Do not use it to state who the gods Valor or Nature are in Teyvat's history.

key: Without Heed for Day nor Night
106.comment: Clash of Kings: Laws of the Board
106.content: Laws of the Board is the temporary buff of Clash of Kings (gameplay): ATK and Elemental Mastery for a short time after an Elemental Skill, extended by a Charged Attack hit. The names echo the rule disputes of the story.

107.content:
Cloudforged (also: Crag-Chiseled Forge): Cloudforged is a 4-star bow added in Version 4.7. Its in-game description calls it a prototype of a standard-issue weapon that the Yuheng commissioned from Blackcliff Forge, after analysing the ancient mechanisms that guarded the adeptal abode on Mount Tianheng. It was a reward of the limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation.

Its archive text is not about the bow itself but about Blackcliff Forge and the semi-legendary founder of the Yun family of smiths.

Appearance: Canon gives no description of the bow's look. Do not invent materials or decoration.

Lore: The item text says the ancients called Mount Tianheng full of gems and the Chasm rich in jade, and that Liyue's key mining and smelting works are in Blackcliff Forge, carved into Tianheng itself.

The Forge was built by hollowing out the mountain into countless workshops, furnaces and soot-blackened connecting tunnels. In the years of war the ancestors of the mountain tribes took shelter there, and long-forgotten passages are said to lead down to an ancient underground realm. According to the Stone Tablet Compilations, the founder of the famed Yun family first carved the dark paths through the mountains, and the Yun house of smiths has since been honoured by later artisans as their progenitor.

Mechanisms and forging were once bound up with the adepti, so the founder was often taken as an adeptal apprentice. The best-known tale says the founder served beside Rex Lapis on campaign and was acknowledged and taught secret mechanical arts by three adepti in turn. Legend claims clouds could be plucked from the sky to mould manses, and decaying wood carved into lifelike birds and beasts; hence the Liyue saying 'the Blackcliff, forged from clouds'. A passage from the annals praises wooden birds that fly for three days without landing.

The text then deflates the legend: cloud-forging is a latter-day play on the family name Yun, 'cloud', though the founder devoted a whole life to the Forge and to teaching craft, and at life's end ascended in heavenly light to become the guardian star of artisanry. Yet the Forge was no adeptal art but was chiselled out hammerstroke by hammerstroke by ordinary artisans over centuries; Deus Auri's contract, it notes, never said mortal resolve could not surpass adeptal miracles. It ends with the founder's maxim that what benefits the people is clever and what does not is clumsy.

Owners: No owner is named in canon. The description frames it as a prototype of an issue weapon for the Yuheng (the office Keqing holds).

Quests: Obtained through the limited-time Version 4.7 event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation, which also gave the refinement material Cam and Cables of Law.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star bow, base ATK 42, Elemental Mastery secondary stat (36). Passive Crag-Chiseled Forge: after Elemental Energy is decreased, the wearer gains 40 to 80 Elemental Mastery (by refinement) for 18s, up to 2 stacks. Refinement uses Cam and Cables of Law instead of duplicate weapons; four came from the event.

108.comment: Cloudforged: Blackcliff Forge and the Yun founder
108.content: Cloudforged's text portrays Blackcliff Forge as a mountain-carved complex of workshops and tunnels, a refuge in wartime and later Liyue's key mining and smelting centre, begun by the founder of the Yun family of smiths. The legend of adeptal teaching coexists with the claim that the Forge was built by ordinary labour.

109.content:
Conch Echoes (also: Conch Echoes (book)): It is a fable, not a record. No character is named beyond nicknames such as "Shorty", and no real place is identified. Its theme is that a leader's authority fails when he fears being seen as flawed, and that a shared symbol of speech should belong to everyone.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of two volumes. Both are sold by Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town.

Lore: Vol. 2: The young man has become pale, green-tinged and stiff, slumped in a heap-laden chair, with the blade fallen where nobody will pick it up. A girl with glasses finds Shorty. He says he saw this coming from the moment the conch was demanded, and that the tyrant, afraid of showing flaws as the adults had, grew suspicious, sleepless and angry until he undid himself. Shorty picks up the nicked, chipped blade, throws it into the sea, and holds the conch to his ear to hear the waves. He proposes a town where the conch belongs to all, and he accepts that today's children will become tomorrow's adults and others may overthrow them.

The text states that the ideal order the children hoped for did not arrive: without anyone to restrain them, the cruelty still in their hearts grew, and some reasoned that if violence could overthrow everything it could take everything. The narration comments that most stories' protagonists need only more patience. Shorty calls the conch a mere toy found on the beach, which suggests the symbol matters less than the agreement behind it.

The handsome young man is never named and is described only by his looks, his blade and his claim to have worked hardest. The blade is dented from years of chopping wood, and the text says he hid its need for care, which is how its decline became a metaphor for his own. The red marks on Shorty's palms from the conch's rope are noted when the girl hands him the shell.

Owners: No owner. It is a commercial book sold in Nasha Town.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 6.0, bought from Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books.

110.comment: Conch Echoes: Shorty and the Conch
110.content: In the fable Conch Echoes, "Shorty" is the smallest of the exiled children and keeps the conch that gives its holder the right to speak. He gives it up to a rival with a blade, lets that rival wreck himself, then throws the blade into the sea and makes the conch common property of a new town. Both are fictional figures with no known canon counterpart.

111.content:
Crane's Echoing Call (also: Cranes Echoing Call): Crane's Echoing Call is a five-star catalyst of Liyue, described in game as a fan carved from pure jade with an ancient aura of adeptal energy swirling around it. Its item story tells of a distant time before Liyue Harbor existed, when refugees begged the adepti for shelter while a horde of maddened monsters pursued them, and how the adeptus Cloud Retainer is said to have saved them. Xianyun, who is Cloud Retainer, wields it.

The story gives three competing versions of the rescue, and the speaker at the end teasingly refuses to say which is true.

Appearance: The description names only a fan of pure jade ringed by adeptal energy. The story's adeptus appears with azure and white feathers, as jade-carved cranes, or with a folding fan in hand, depending on the version. Xianyun's own crane form, described in her profile, is not described in the item text.

Lore: In the distant past, before the harbor city existed, even the adepti's abodes were burned by the war of the gods. Survivors who lost everything fled to the mountains and begged the adepti for shelter, hounded by countless monsters that had lost their senses. These monsters came like a flood and were, in truth, mourning the fallen master they had once revered, the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. Only a few yaksha stood between the refugees and catastrophe, fighting for days until white clothes turned scarlet and scarlet turned black.

The story says the tale has since branched into versions. In one, an adeptus with azure and white feathers burst from the clouds like a gale and, solitary and proud, vanquished the apparently endless tide. In another, two jade cranes hurtled down in a hail of sigils, then turned out to be an adeptus in the air with a folding fan. In a third, the ancestors only heard a crane's cry and the monsters turned to ash like dust in sunlight. All versions credit Cloud Retainer, and Liyue folk choose their words about her with respect.

The close shifts to a spoken scene: a character addresses a listener who asked about "such distant matters", says the tale would take eight or nine hours, tells them to pull up a chair, and then scolds them for trying to slink away while distracted. The voice is not named in the text; the pattern of speech fits Cloud Retainer, who refers to herself as "one", but treat that as an inference. For Xianyun's own history (her work with machines and her crane form) use her file.

Owners: Wielder: Xianyun (Cloud Retainer), shown with the ascended version in her character demo and Collected Miscellany. The item text does not name an owner.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star catalyst from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 49, secondary stat ATK 3.6%. Passive "Cloudfall Axiom": after the wielder lands a Plunging Attack, all nearby party members' Plunging Attacks deal 28-80% more DMG for 20 seconds, and their Plunging hits restore the wielder 2.5-3.5 Energy every 0.7 seconds, even off the field (refinements 1 to 5). The wiki lists its base ATK among the highest in the game.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): suit it to storytelling and the shifting nature of legend; a character may tell the rescue tale with deliberate vagueness and a tendency to ramble.

112.comment: Crane's Echoing Call: Cloud Retainer legend
112.content: Cloud Retainer is an adeptus of Mt. Aocang and Jueyun Karst, said in legend to have rescued refugees from a monster tide long before Liyue Harbor. She is also known as Xianyun in the mortal world and can take a crane form. The item story gives three versions of the rescue and does not decide between them.

113.content:
Crimson Agate (also: Crimson Agates): Crimson Agate is a crystal found on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. It forms when concentrated life force combines with an energy unique to Dragonspine, and it is ideal nourishment for the Frostbearing Tree.

The crystals are offered to the Frostbearing Tree, much as Oculi are offered to the Statues of The Seven, to earn rewards. They lie in the open, in chests marked by a dark red glow, and as rewards for Crimson Wishes.

The archive description tells a short history. The nail that froze Dragonspine shattered the tree's trunk and canopy into frozen fragments. Long after, a black dragon fell into the valley and its blood seeped into the ley lines. Longer after that, someone broke the icy shackles and the ancient tree, having absorbed that crimson, sprouted anew.

It entered the game in Version 1.2 with Dragonspine. Its Chinese name is rendered by the wiki as Crimson Chalcedony, which is a translation note, not a separate item.

Appearance: A red crystal. Overworld agates show a map icon and sound like Oculi do, and chests holding one are surrounded by a dark red aura.

Lore: The item text frames the agates as the tree's nutrition after it was shattered and frozen by the Skyfrost Nail. The crimson is the blood of a black dragon that fell into Wyrmrest Valley, carried through the ley lines.

The Lavawalker artifact text separately says the Lavawalker made a circlet from Crimson Agate to withstand heat in Mare Jivari, so the crystal appears outside Dragonspine in canon. The text gives no explanation.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: 80 agates can be found in the overworld and chests, enough to raise the Frostbearing Tree from Offering Level 1 to 9 before Crimson Wishes, which unlock at Level 8. Crimson Wishes keep giving agates until the tree reaches Level 12.

114.comment: Crimson Agate: Crimson Agate and the Frostbearing Tree
114.content: Crimson Agates are the offering that makes the Frostbearing Tree of Dragonspine grow. The tree was shattered and frozen when the Skyfrost Nail descended, and later absorbed the blood of a black dragon through the ley lines.

115.content:
Crimson Moon's Semblance (also: Crimson Moon's Semblance polearm): Crimson Moon's Semblance is a 5-star polearm (released in Version 4.6) whose text recalls an ancient Khaenri'ahn dynasty that revered the crimson moon. Its description calls it a keen-edged weapon with a luster as dazzling as the crimson moon, once regarded by that dynasty as a ritual object that could bridge two worlds. Arlecchino is its signature wielder in gameplay.

Nobody in the item text remembers the beliefs and ceremonies tied to the weapon; the dynasty is described as a bygone age. The story is a lament about the fall of the Crimson Moon's followers and the survival of only the epithet "Balemoon."

Appearance: A polearm with a bright, keen edge, its sheen compared to the crimson moon. When Arlecchino wields it, it transforms into a scythe during her Normal Attacks, Charged Attack and Elemental Skill. In her "Masque of the Red Death" state it shows a red aura running down the staff (gameplay presentation).

Lore: The item story is a sombre account of Khaenri'ah's old royal clan and the Crimson Moon, not of the weapon's own forging.

It opens with an invocation to the High Lord of the Nobles of Khaenri'ah: the crimson-red moon has long since fallen into the abyssal firmament, and the blindness of that bloodline has ended the line. A cup of wine is offered to the lord.

Per the story, in an ancient era, before the dark sun lit the underground, an ancient and glorious clan ruled the kingdom. Dogmatic priests persuaded the muddle-minded king that the Crimson Moon's remnants in the sky ruled all, because the color of moonlight flows beneath mortal flesh and the darkness at the bottom of the abyss would also come from it. The king was therefore to take the name of the Crimson Moon and judge fate by the light and flame of two worlds. The court sought transcendent individuals to build countless glorious towers and prayed for the long-dead Crimson Moon to save them. Astrologers branded as heretics then glimpsed, in the inverted image of the false sky, the origin of the world's fate. Flames of doubt and fury spread through the dreamless realm and burned even the moonlight-hued palace.

By the time of the "blackened sun" (the Eclipse Dynasty), the Crimson Moon's name had faded along with the crimson that had flowed; only the epithet "Balemoon" survived. Neither those who suffered the curse nor those not yet tainted by fate would again call themselves followers of the moon. The few survivors hid in the shadows and longed for the Crimson Moon to repay their vengeance, but that never came, and the dark sun fell to the same ignorance and arrogance. When destruction (the Cataclysm) neared again, only mocking moonlight fell upon the shadow of a sun long burnt to ash. The closing verse addresses fate as submitting to a tyrannical usurper (the wiki links this to the Heavenly Principles) and speaks of mocking the destiny "she" wove (linked to Sonnet), until the last shadow of the ashen sun burns away the old world and the Crimson Moon witnesses an immaculate dawn. Those links are the wiki's annotations on the text, not stated outright by it.

Owners: Arlecchino, the Fourth Fatui Harbinger and head of the House of the Hearth, is its signature wielder.

Arlecchino is a descendant of the Crimson Moon Dynasty and is titled "Dire Balemoon," echoing the story's word. The weapon's text does not mention her, and canon does not spell out how the weapon relates to her in story terms.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a 5-star Polearm with a base ATK of 48 and a secondary stat of CRIT Rate. Its passive, Ashen Sun's Shadow, grants a Bond of Life equal to 25% of Max HP when a Charged Attack hits an opponent (at most once every 14 seconds). While the wielder has a Bond of Life they gain a DMG Bonus, and a further bonus if the Bond of Life is at least 30% of Max HP. The bonuses rise with refinement, and Bonds of Life from this weapon can stack. It was released on 2024-04-24 through Weapon Event Wishes and is also available in Chronicled Wishes.

Its ascension materials include the Goblet of the Pristine Sea items, Hilt materials from a boss, and gear-type common materials. Its passive name, "Ashen Sun's Shadow," echoes the burned-out sun in its story.

116.comment: Crimson Moon's Semblance: Crimson Moon Dynasty and Balemoon
116.content: The weapon's story presents the Crimson Moon Dynasty as an ancient royal clan of Khaenri'ah whose priests tied the throne to the Crimson Moon. Its fall left only the epithet "Balemoon" and a few survivors hiding from the later dark sun.

key: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set
117.content:
Crimson Witch of Flames (also: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set, Witch's Flower of Blaze, Witch's Ever-Burning Plume, Witch's End Time, Witch's Heart Flames, Witch's Scorching Hat): Crimson Witch of Flames is a Pyro artifact set (4 and 5 star) built around the story of a young woman who lost her hopes and loved ones in a calamity and became a witch who burned monsters and demons. Its texts call her 'the Crimson Witch of Flame'. Later canon (Archon Quest, 2.1) identifies her as the Fatui Harbinger Signora, once a maiden of Mondstadt. The set is earned in the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula.

The five pieces are Witch's Flower of Blaze, Witch's Ever-Burning Plume, Witch's End Time, Witch's Heart Flames and Witch's Scorching Hat. Read in order, they sketch a single life: a student, a disaster, a path of fire, and a person who cannot see how much she has destroyed.

Appearance: Pyro-themed relics: a flower that survives flame, a never-dying feather, a small timepiece holding a hot liquid, a flame-spitting urn holding liquid fire, and a witch's tall hat with a broad brim.

The hat is the classic pointed witch's hat with a large brim; the text says the brim blocked her sight. The timepiece is described as a small vessel of high-temperature liquid, said to be the molten souls of evil spirits.

Lore: Per the item texts, a crisis centuries ago took the maiden's loved ones, her past and her promised future. From it the Crimson Witch of Flame was born, dreaming of burning away all the demons in the world. Her fire touched only monsters and demons, yet people shut their windows and tried to drive her off. She wanted no comfort; only the birds beside her understood. Historians were loath to remember her.

A common flower is described as strangely able to withstand her flames, a hint that painful and beautiful memories were two sides of one coin. The Heart Flames text says rumour held she gave up her mortal body to become liquid fire, and that love and longing once lived in her before the fire burned that part away. The Scorching Hat text ends on the image of a witch who burned on, blind to the scale of her destruction and unwilling to look at her burnt face in the water.

Two details tie the texts to named places. The End Time text says the timepiece was a Hydro timepiece given to her before the calamity; one cycle was the time needed to finish her study at the Akademiya (the Sumeru Akademiya), and by the time the countdown ended and she came home, its previous owner (the giver) had become a casualty of the crisis. The Scorching Hat text says the hat let her hone her Pyro skills while still an apprentice.

The set text itself never names her. The link to Signora comes from elsewhere: the Archon Quest 'Duel Before the Throne' (2.1) presents Signora as the Crimson Witch of Flame/Embers, and Signora's profile items tell of a Mondstadt maiden named Rosalyne who studied at the Akademiya and received a Hydro timepiece from Rostam of the Knights of Favonius before she left. The wiki's trivia for the set treats it as the story of La Signora, historically known as the Crimson Witch of Flame.

The texts and the Signora story agree on the broad arc: a student at the Akademiya, a gift to count the time away, a return to find the giver dead after a crisis, then a path of fire against monsters. Signora's profile items further say that the fire nearly consumed her until she met Pierro and received a Cryo Delusion, after which she became La Signora of the Fatui Harbingers. That later stage is not part of this set's text; keep it out of any scene that treats the set as only an old relic.

Owners: By the texts, the relics belonged to or were touched by the Crimson Witch of Flame. Canon (the 2.1 Archon Quest and Signora's profile) identifies her with Signora, whose original name was Rosalyne. The relics found in domains are treated in game as remnants; no canon scene shows Signora carrying them.

Status as of 7.1: Signora died in Inazuma during 'Duel Before the Throne' (2.1); her Harbinger seat remains vacant as of 7.1. Characters who know only the artifact texts know only the legend of a nameless 'Crimson Witch of Flame'; the identification with Signora is not common knowledge.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat these as relics with a tragic legend, not a trophy. A character who handles them may sense warmth or tell an old story of a maiden who became a witch. A character who does not know the Archon Quest revelation should not call the witch Signora.

Gameplay: Gameplay (game mechanics, not in-world fact). A 4-star and 5-star set from the Domain of Blessing Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula. The 2-piece bonus gives +15% Pyro DMG Bonus. The 4-piece bonus raises Overloaded, Burning and Burgeon DMG by 40% and Vaporize and Melt DMG by 15%, and each Elemental Skill use adds to the 2-piece Pyro bonus for 10 seconds, up to 3 stacks.

118.comment: Crimson Witch of Flames: Crimson Witch of Flame legend
118.content:
The 'Crimson Witch of Flame' of the artifact texts is a legendary witch who burned monsters and demons after a calamity cost her everything. The texts do not name her. A student at the Akademiya, she was hated and feared by ordinary people although her fire touched only monsters. Historians were loath to remember her.

Signora's profile (revealed in 2.1) identifies her as the witch. Only people who have the Archon Quest knowledge can link the two.

119.comment: Crimson Witch of Flames: Witch's End Time
119.content: The timepiece was given to the maiden before the calamity and counted the time of her studies at the Akademiya. Signora's profile says its giver was Rostam; the set text itself says only that its previous owner became a casualty of the crisis.

120.content:
Cryo Gnosis (also: Tsaritsa's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Cryo Archon): The Cryo Gnosis is the Gnosis of the Cryo Archon. It is held by Anastasya, the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, and is the only one of the seven Gnoses that never had to be collected by the Fatui. Like every Gnosis, it is a divine focus that resembles a chess piece and strengthens its bearer's elemental power. Each Archon's Gnosis also links them to Celestia.

As of Version 7.1, the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses: her own Cryo Gnosis plus the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses her Harbingers gathered. Only the Pyro Gnosis is missing. In 7.1 she revealed that all seven Gnoses were formed from the remains of the Third Descender. She wants them for two reasons: to amplify her power for a confrontation with the Heavenly Principles, and to open a seal the Third Descender left beneath Zapolyarny Palace.

Appearance: Like every Gnosis it resembles a gleaming chess piece and normally rests within its Archon's chest. No canon text describes its individual shape or colour, so do not invent details.

A Gnosis can be drawn out of an Archon by force or materialized at will.
In 7.1 the Tsaritsa's six Gnoses were shown outside her body, set as energy nodes marking the edges of a field she raised inside her palace. It is the first time the Cryo Gnosis is seen working alongside the others.

Lore: Origin: Saarelainen, the Third Descender, was Anastasya's lover and the ancestor of the Khaenri'ahns. After the Heavenly Principles erased her existence, he bargained with them for her resurrection and for the safety of their descendants. In exchange, he agreed to let his remains be split into seven pieces to consolidate the Heavenly Principles' rule. Those pieces are the Gnoses. The Cryo Gnosis held by the Cryo Archon is therefore part of the body of the man the Tsaritsa loved, though the Heavenly Principles erased him and every memory related to him from her mind (and, through Irminsul, from the world).
In Light and Shadow, Intertwined, the Tsaritsa tells the Traveler that the Gnoses have a powerful elemental affinity and amplify their bearers. Because they come from the Third Descender rather than from Teyvat's own system, she says, their full potential could let a god go beyond the limits of their authority. She calls this a necessary step toward facing the Heavenly Principles, since the power of The Seven alone "cannot shake the foundations of the world." She also says the Third Descender's seal beneath the palace responds only to a Gnosis. She guesses that it might open once all his scattered remains are gathered again.

The Tsaritsa reasons that the missing Pyro Gnosis, as a remnant of the Third Descender, cannot coexist with the Ley Lines for long and will eventually be ejected and found. Earlier, in Mistilteinn (7.0), The Jester (Pierro) described the Gnoses as a key bargaining chip for when she confronts the Heavenly Principles. In Delusion (7.1) he said she had already amassed enough power to strike at Teyvat's rules even without all seven. In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting, Ronova threatens the Traveler by pointing to the Third Descender's remains, "the playthings of the gods for centuries now", as a precedent.

Owners: Current holder: Anastasya, the Tsaritsa and Cryo Archon, at Zapolyarny Palace in Snezhnograd.

Canon implies that the seven Gnoses went to the original members of The Seven after the Archon War. The first Cryo Archon was the Belyi Tsar, who ruled Snezhnaya from about 2,000 to 500 years ago. Anastasya succeeded him when he died during the Cataclysm. Canon does not narrate how the Cryo Gnosis passed between them (see uncertainties).

The Tsaritsa added the other Gnoses to her own. Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti by force and received the Geo Gnosis from Zhongli by contract. Dottore obtained the Electro and Dendro Gnoses from Nahida. Arlecchino brought the Hydro Gnosis, which Neuvillette gave her as a diplomatic gift. The Pyro Gnosis was never taken. It was lost when Irminsul burned; the Traveler told the Tsaritsa that, according to Mavuika, it has returned to the Ley Lines, and it has not been found.

Gameplay: Gameplay: the Cryo Gnosis is a story object only. Players cannot obtain or equip it, and it has no stats. It appears only in Archon Quest cutscenes and dialogue.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Cryo Gnosis as a state secret and a divine organ, not a trinket. Ordinary Snezhnayans and rank-and-file Fatui would at most know that the Tsaritsa is gathering Gnoses. Very few people know that the Gnoses are a dead Descender's remains. Do not show the Gnosis being lent, stolen or casually displayed as of 7.1.

If a scene needs the Tsaritsa's full power, remember her own words: the Gnoses are only one part of it, and her own insight over a thousand years matters too. An Archon also keeps elemental power without a Gnosis, so taking it away would not leave her powerless.

121.content: In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), the Tsaritsa hosted Rhinedottir for tea while the Traveler, Dainsleif and Pierro fought Ronova. Unnoticed, she had placed her six Gnoses, the Cryo Gnosis among them, as nodes around the hall. Using Cryo amplified to its limit, she bent "the bounds of Reason" enough to slow time inside the room, though not to freeze it. Rhinedottir missed the window she and Ronova had arranged to undo Ronova's curse of death without the Heavenly Principles' monitoring noticing. Celestia then reclaimed Ronova's authority for abuse. Rhinedottir called this power beyond what a god should have. The Tsaritsa answered that the Gnoses were only one aspect, and that she knew the trick would not work on Rhinedottir twice.

122.comment: Cryo Gnosis: Third Descender's seal and the Gnoses
122.content: Beneath Zapolyarny Palace lies a large crystalline seal left by the Third Descender before the Heavenly Principles killed him. The Heavenly Principles seem never to have noticed it. The Belyi Tsar guarded it first, and the Tsaritsa inherited the duty. Every attempt to open it has failed, and only a Gnosis draws any response from it. The Tsaritsa believes all seven Gnoses, his reunited remains, are needed. She showed it to the Traveler in Light and Shadow, Intertwined. As of 7.1 it remains sealed because the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

123.content:
Crystal Chunk (also: Crystal Chunks, Crystal Ore): Crystal Chunk is a turquoise crystal, an uncut ore taken from Crystal Ore nodes in caves, mines and mountains across Teyvat. Its item text says only professional craftsmanship can bring out its true value. Smiths use it in forging, chiefly for Mystic Enhancement Ore.

It is found in the wild, including Stormterror's Lair, and can also come from shops and expeditions.

Appearance: Raw, uncut turquoise crystals, grown in clusters inside breakable ore nodes. They are plainer than the blue Magical Crystal Chunk, whose crystals have been altered by the Ley Lines.

Lore: The in-game description calls it an uncut crystal whose real value emerges only through professional craftsmanship. A longer form of the text names this clear rock a precious gift of the land, useful as a valuable weapon-making material. Nothing more is said about its origin.

Item text contrasts it with the Magical Crystal Chunk, which Ley Line energy has eroded so that ordinary methods cannot process it. Crystal Chunks are the ordinary kind that a smith can work directly.

Gameplay: Gameplay note, not in-world lore: breaking a node gives 1 to 3 chunks, and nodes respawn after several days. Mystic Enhancement Ore, a weapon enhancement material, is mostly forged from them. The Chasm's underground mines also contain nodes.

Nodes can also spawn in places called Mining Outcrops, where a Magical Crystal Ore node appears alongside ordinary ones. Expeditions in Whispering Woods, Dadaupa Gorge and Yaoguang Shoal can reward chunks too.

Scene use: A miner, smith or traveller can handle chunks as a common raw material. Nothing in canon ties it to a person or story, so avoid inventing a legend for it.

124.content:
Crystal Core (also: Crystal Cores, crystalfly core): Crystal Core is the core of a crystal butterfly, a crystalfly. Its item text says it absorbs elemental energy that has escaped into the atmosphere. It is obtained by catching a crystalfly, not by fighting it.

Moonglow Fireflies also yield it.

Appearance: A small glowing core taken from a crystalfly, one of the elemental butterflies seen across Teyvat in several types, including Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro, Pyro and Cryo.

Lore: The item description presents it as the core of a crystal butterfly that takes in elemental energy that had escaped into the atmosphere. The wiki describes crystalflies as elemental life-forms. Their cores therefore stand for loose elemental energy gathered into a small body.

The wiki records that Nahida remarks a Pyro crystalfly could easily be mistaken for a firefly because both glow. It also notes that crystalflies do not appear when it is raining, so they always appear in Dragonspine, where it does not rain.

Gameplay: Gameplay note, not in-world lore: killing a crystalfly makes it vanish with no drop; catching it gives one core. Without certain wildlife talents they flee on approach, and a caught one respawns after 24 hours.

Cores are spent in crafting and ascension. Crystalflies of every element share the same material.

Scene use: A traveller may carefully catch a glowing butterfly for its core. Keep the explanation to the item text; canon gives no deeper mechanism.

125.content:
Customs of Liyue (also: Liyue Customs): Customs of Liyue is a three-volume book about Liyue's traditions, originally compiled by Fadhlan, a scholar from Sumeru living in Liyue, then edited by local scholars and published. It is described as one of Liyue's bestsellers. The volumes cover the wedding flower ball, the Rite of Descension in which the Geo Archon receives his people, and the cultural place of the Silk Flower and its perfumes.

Much of the commentary is the outsider's viewpoint of a Sumeru scholar, who contrasts Liyue's practical, prosperity-minded devotion with Sumeru's ecstatic scholar-sages and who declines in the last lines to guess at the Geo Archon's inner feelings.

Appearance: Three short essays headed Flower Ball, Receiving God and Silk Flowers. The tone is that of a gently wry travel-writer's survey, mixing legend with practical observation, such as Millelith injury logs.

Lore: - Vol. 1, Flower Ball: at Liyue weddings the bride tosses a flower ball to the guests; catching it is said to bring a year of good luck. Wealthier families use silk balls, poorer families paper or cloth.
- Vol. 2, Receiving God: the Rite of Descension is the most iconic Liyue ceremony, at which the Geo Archon descends to deliver his proclamations. In the Qixing era a member of the Qixing hosts it.
- Vol. 3, Silk Flowers: the Silk Flower is used for silk and perfume. Rural legend credits an adeptus on Mt. Aocang with teaching mortals perfume making, and the flower is a symbol of Rex Lapis.

- Vol. 1 notes that the Millelith's security logs attribute roughly as many injuries per year to flower ball tossing as to monster attacks. It gives two possible origins: Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum, or the Salt God Havria, a gentle god ousted in the Archon War and murdered by one of her own followers, said to have handed flowers to her people as comfort. Her remains are thought to lie in the ruins of Sal Terrae, and her followers may have spread the custom across Liyue.
- Vol. 2 says early farmers chose representatives to greet and see off the Geo Archon, who made predictions that set the year's work. After the Archon War, Liyue Harbor's merchants prized his predictions above ore, and travelled home to hear them. Only a Qixing member may host the rite. The author contrasts Liyue's worldly gains from divine guidance with the raving sages of Sumeru's rainforests, and notes that the Seven's paths can diverge.
- Vol. 3 says the Silk Flower is cultivated in a special strain for luxury perfume, offered first to Rex Lapis. An unwritten rule makes it impolite to ask a woman about her perfume, but an admirer who correctly identifies it tactfully may win her favour. Wild Silk Flowers have nearly vanished from rural areas because of mining and geographic change; the remaining few are tended by reclusive adepti.

- Vol. 3 tells of the adeptus who appeared as a graceful illuminated bird to a young woman bathing in a spring and taught her to prepare fragrant oils, and says countless versions of the story exist. It also says the author once saw a Statue of the Seven accept a distinctly feminine offering, while declining to comment on the Archon's feelings.
- Merchants attribute their Silk Flower varieties to chance meetings with Rex Lapis or gifts from adepti, a sales habit the author calls tasteless.

- The wiki notes the flower ball custom echoes a real-world Zhuang tradition of throwing embroidered silk balls; this is a real-world parallel and not in-universe canon.
- Vol. 2's description of the Qixing as intermediaries is a pre-7.1 snapshot of the rite as written; compare current Liyue entries on how the rite is run now.

Owners: No individual owner. Vol. 1 is on a shelf at Wanwen Bookhouse and is a reward from Soraya. Vol. 2 is on Ningguang's desk in the Jade Chamber and appears during Zhongli's story quest Sal Flore. Vol. 3 is sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse in Liyue Harbor.

Gameplay: Game note: a collectible book collection read for lore only.

126.comment: Customs of Liyue: Flower Ball Custom
126.content: At Liyue weddings the bride throws a flower ball; the guest who catches it is said to enjoy good luck for a year, whatever their situation. Wealthy families use silk-flower balls and poor families paper or cloth. Origin is disputed between Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum and the followers of the ancient Salt God Havria. Millelith logs count many injuries from it.

127.comment: Customs of Liyue: Silk Flower Perfume
127.content: In Customs of Liyue Vol. 3 the Silk Flower is a Liyue luxury, used for silk and perfume. Perfume is a delicate social topic; guessing a woman's scent tactfully is a courting skill. Legend says an adeptus on Mt. Aocang taught the art, and the flower is one of Rex Lapis' symbols.

128.content:
Dawning Frost (also: Nocturnal Dreams, Dawning Frost catalyst): A silver-forged ritual vessel, pure and without blemish, said to be a sacred relic passed down among the priestesses of the far north. A 4-star catalyst of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.1.

Its text follows a mother's prophetic dream.

Appearance: A catalyst described as a silver-forged ritual vessel, unblemished. The text mentions a silvery-white talisman worn at the chest, but does not say it is this object.

Lore: The item text is a warning and a dream: a mother tells her child, Avrelian, never to set foot in Nod-Krai and not to be taken in by "that fool's dream of Elysium".

She is the woman once worshipped as the Maiden, living far from her homeland (Hiisi Island). She says a thousand-year-old curse runs in his blood and no earthly paradise has been built for mortals under the moon. Pregnant, she is troubled by visions of the fate of her homeland.

The dream cycles through an age: seeds of life fall from silver branches into a ruined city; featherless upright creatures enjoy wisdom, then greed, hatred and strife follow while divine envoys watch silently. The kings of the lands test the eternal heavens and their towers fall in flame. After a thousand years a golden city rises (Hyperborea) and mortals, longing for the vacant throne of the world, try to dissolve the line between man and god. The draconic kings of flame plunge into the Abyss and the tide swallows a white-stone empire.

Out of the dark she hears a familiar, compassionate voice that promises to end the warriors of the land and raise a boundless Elysium in their place, "not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role". The dream always shatters at that promise. She wakes in pale morning light, her fingers on the talisman, her hand on her belly, and asks her unborn child why it stirs, whether it senses her fear. The text does not say whose voice it is, nor resolve whether the dream is memory, prophecy or both.

Owners: No wielder is named; the description ties it to the priestesses of the far north.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42, CRIT DMG secondary. Passive Nocturnal Dreams gives Elemental Mastery for 10 seconds after a Charged Attack hits, and a separate boost after an Elemental Skill hits. Released in Version 6.1.

How {{char}} behaves: Use as an heirloom-style vessel with hushed religious weight. Nod-Krai folk and Scion descendants might recognise it; keep the dream as a text artefact, not a verified record of what happened.

129.content: Nocturnal Dreams is the weapon's passive, named for the prophetic dreams in its text. Mechanics are in the gameplay section.

130.content:
Deathmatch (also: Deathmatch polearm, the gladiator's spear): Deathmatch is a four-star crimson polearm, part of the Gnostic Hymn series from the Battle Pass. Its item story follows a gladiator who fought for blood, then for the young master he loved, and who died by the blade of a red-haired maiden at his last performance. The wiki identifies that maiden as Vennessa and the master as Eberhart.

Item text calls it a gladiator's priceless treasure, with a point stained by the blood of countless beasts and men. It is a Mondstadt-linked story weapon, tied by the wiki to the Gladiator's Finale artifact set.

Appearance: A sharp crimson polearm with an ice-cold tip. The text mentions nothing else about its shaft or decoration, so do not invent any.

Lore: The story is a duelist's tragedy. The polearm watched the valor of a gladiator whose tip was often wet with the blood of his foes while the crowd applauded. Freedom always seemed near and never came. When his master told him the promised number of victories had been met, he offered the spear as a parting gift and asked him to fight on as a free man, for glory, for the gladiator and for himself. Over many years the beasts and men the spear felled were too many to count, and the weapon was called undefeated, but the gladiator's heart belonged to his young master.

In his final performance, the gladiator's weapon fell to the sand when the red-haired maiden's burning blade pierced his heart. As he fell he looked toward his master's seat, which was empty apart from a toppled wine goblet and silver platter, and asked whether Master Eberhart had liked the performance. His dying words say that at first he fought for himself, for blood and battle-lust, and later killed for his master; he added that people can fight like wild beasts without care only for the sake of others, and that she, who fought for her people and not for herself, would surely understand.

The wiki links the maiden to Vennessa and the master to Eberhart; the item text itself gives only the master's name and calls the killer a red-haired maiden. It also notes that the story ties into the Gladiator's Finale artifact set. The empty seat is the story's cruelest detail: the man who gave the order to fight on is not even there to watch him die, and the text never says whether he fled or simply left.

Owners: The gladiator of the item story (historical.unnamed-gladiator), who received it from his master as a parting gift. No later owner is named.

In promotional material Chevreuse wields it in her character demo, her Collected Miscellany video and the Version 4.3 'Roses and Muskets' trailer; that is presentation, not a canon statement that she owns it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): obtained through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn. Base ATK 41, secondary stat CRIT Rate 8%. Passive 'Gladiator': with at least two opponents nearby, ATK and DEF each rise by 16-32% across refinements 1-5; with fewer than two, ATK rises by 24-48% instead.

The wiki notes that the passive state is updated only while its wielder is on the field and keeps the last state after they are switched out.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a symbol of loyalty that outlasts freedom, and of a person who stops fighting for himself and starts fighting for someone else. A character holding it can reasonably speak of arena life and of the cost of a master's applause.

131.content: The Deathmatch story's gladiator was freed by promise but chose to keep fighting for his young master Eberhart. He was killed in the arena by a red-haired maiden, whom the wiki identifies as Vennessa. His name is not given in canon.

132.content:
Deepwood Memories (also: Labyrinth Wayfarer, Scholar of Vines, A Time of Insight, Lamp of the Lost, Laurel Coronet): Deepwood Memories is a Sumeru rainforest artifact set (Version 3.0, Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain). Its five pieces are fragments of old forest legends: a labyrinth of roots and water, a lord of the forest and the maiden who inherited his crown, a huntress with a white bow, and friends who fought forgetting.

Nothing in the set is dated. It reads as a mix of oral legend and a few personal confessions, and no piece names its speaker.

Lore: When the lord of the forest was born, the king of trees gave them a crown, which passed to the first maiden to follow in the lord's footsteps. She took in lost children and taught them the hunt, the walk through dreams and love for the forest's plants and creatures. Some became guardians who patrolled the woods and lit bonfires against the dark. One stayed behind, hunting the shadows until she dreamed a great dream of the labyrinth and hunt that covered every other dream of the forest, and then she disappeared with it.

The Laurel Coronet gives the forest's origin: the god of trees made a forest among the sands and first built a device to call rain; moonlight on the water drew a labyrinth, and the labyrinth birthed a tiger named Viaghara, the first lord. Pomegranate seeds became forest spirits, who were allowed to share the labyrinth by a pact. The last lord died defending the nurseries of life and a large whiskered cat took the name. A Time of Insight records the immortal lord melting into the forest and friends who vowed to remind one another of their forms to defeat death, until forgetfulness struck. Lamp of the Lost tells of a desert prince who fled to the rainforest and was accepted by its dream.

Scholar of Vines tells two stories. A servant girl, the lord's most virtuous, understood beasts and moonlight poetry; her teaching thinned like tiger blood. In the "years of the ominous moon" a blind swordsman followed his white-armoured brother into the dark forest, found a white relic of the woods, and lost his power to wish before the huntress reached him. The pieces also include the speaker of A Time of Insight, who plans to capture dream spirits and hire sellswords to give a friend with brain damage dreams of their shared past. The wiki ties the labyrinth and Viaghara to the forest god Rukkhadevata's rainforest and says the final lord died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, but the item does not name those events.

The maiden's story ends with a doubled loss: the dreams she left behind spread through the people's tales in many forms, yet the best-known tales had nothing to do with her, and the name they use is the name of the crown, not hers. All she kept was her true name, "a handful of water that reflected the moonlight", and the golden flower from the crown. Laurel Coronet gives the laws of the forest as a cycle, in which fruit feeds beasts and beasts become fruit, and the cat who inherited the lord's title, though it "could not match even an iota" of the old lord's might, keeps the promise not to harm the tree spirits.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a set from the Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain (4 and 5 star) and its strongbox. 2-piece: Dendro DMG Bonus +15%. 4-piece: after Elemental Skills or Bursts hit, the target's Dendro RES is lowered by 30% for 8s, even if the wearer is off-field. Released in 3.0; no later change is listed.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present these as half-remembered rainforest legends, not as history. Treat the forest lords, the maiden and the huntress as unnamed.

133.content:
The flower piece of Deepwood Memories: a gold-plated flower from the crown of the lord of the forest. It tells of the first maiden who followed the lord, took in lost children, taught them the hunt and the walk through dreams, and whose lessons produced guardians who patrol the woods. One stayed until she eroded into a vast dream of the labyrinth and hunt.

Only she and those who knew the forest lord's teaching could pass the maze to the endless hunting ground; the whispers that preach death were lost inside it. After she vanished, fragments of her dream entered the tales of her descendants and the crown's name replaced hers.

134.content:
The plume piece: an emerald leaf as fluffy as a feather, plucked from a forest scholar's raiment. Two verses: the years of the lord of the labyrinth, with a servant girl who read the poetry of moonlight, and the years of the ominous moon, with a blind swordsman, a white relic and a huntress.

The girl's teaching: "that which comes from the forest must return to it", so whoever follows nature need not fear death. The blind swordsman is described as obsessed with swordsmanship, gentle, and dogmatic about justice. The verse ends with a glimpse in nightmare of a dark longsword and red blooming in the water.

135.comment: Deepwood Memories: A Time of Insight
135.content:
The sands piece: a timepiece that holds mustard seeds instead of sand, used by those following the way of the wise. Its verses say the lord of the forest was immortal, melting into the forest at death. Then a speaker whose friend suffers from forgetfulness plans to capture dream spirits to remind them of their shared past.

The speaker argues that souls are void concepts and memories must return to the land, so the answer is for friends to remind one another and keep everyone's image alive, defeating the natural cycle. Their plan relies on a scientist expelled by the academy, on dream-controlling forest inhabitants, and on sellswords who "once did much for me".

136.comment: Deepwood Memories: Lamp of the Lost
136.content:
The goblet piece: a desert-style oil lamp that has sprouted glowing green leaves. It belonged to a prince of the decaying desert kingdoms. He tells of his father falling from a tower while chasing a falcon, of burying a lover, of becoming a refugee, and of a rainforest that accepted him after a huntress with a white bow hunted him each night.

The text calls the time after the fall of "the lord of folly" an age of tiny tyrants raising temples and walls on ruins. The prince meant to conquer the rainforest "like a Rishboland Tiger" but was conquered by quiet moonlight, and learned the murmurs of trees and the whispering of tigers.

137.content:
The circlet piece: a crown given by the deity of plants, an heirloom of the royal house of the labyrinth, passed at last to the king's attendant. Its verses describe the cycle of life and death, the god of trees creating a forest among the sands, the first rain-calling device, the tiger Viaghara and the labyrinth, and the forest spirits' pact.

Beneath the first Vasara Tree the lord of the forest made a pact with the divine to share the labyrinth with the forest spirits. Later the sun's light was covered and the water was corrupted; the final forest lord died defending life's nurseries, and a large whiskered cat took the title and kept the promise.

138.content:
Dendro Gnosis (also: Gnosis of Sumeru, Dendro Archon's Gnosis, Kusanali's Gnosis, Nahida's Gnosis): The Dendro Gnosis is Sumeru's Gnosis, one of seven chess-piece-like divine foci held by The Seven, carried inside the Archon's chest. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata used it to build and power the Akasha. In 3.2 Nahida (Lesser Lord Kusanali) gave it to the Fatui Harbinger Dottore in exchange for knowledge about the "false sky", and shut the Akasha down. Dottore brought it to the Tsaritsa in Snezhnaya, and as of 7.1 she holds it with five other Gnoses. Nahida is still the Dendro Archon without it.

Lore: Rukkhadevata built the Akasha during the Cataclysm to pool human wisdom against the forbidden knowledge polluting Irminsul, and it ran on the Dendro Gnosis. In 3.2 the Balladeer tried again and again to tear the Gnosis from Nahida's chest. Nahida then combined it with the Electro Gnosis she won from him to reach Rukkhadevata's last memory. Afterwards Dottore asked for it, arguing that Sumeru would have no use for it once the Akasha was shut down, and offered knowledge in return. She accepted, because as God of Wisdom she would not choose ignorance.

Nahida's character story "Gnosis" says Dottore counted on her curiosity and sense of duty. To her a Gnosis was only a core that gathers elemental power as she wills, so she wondered why a god would want them all. She later told the Traveler the deal was both a punishment for Dottore and knowledge she could not refuse. Dottore presented this Gnosis and the Electro one to the Tsaritsa as trophies (his memory in Anomalous Tree Marrow III, 6.6).

Consequences: The Akasha could not run without the Gnosis, so Nahida shut it down for good. Akasha Terminals became useless and dreams came back to Sumeru. Nahida keeps her divine throne and the Dendro Authority. She has also used other Gnoses: the Electro Gnosis briefly in 3.2, and the Pyro Gnosis to burn Irminsul in 6.6.

In 6.6, when Dottore corrupted Irminsul, Sumeru's scholars planned to restart the Akasha but had nothing to power it without the Dendro Gnosis, and looked for a substitute. In the end the reconfigured Aaru system took over Irminsul's role.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa (Anastasya) holds it in Snezhnaya, one of her six Gnoses; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

She collects the Gnoses to amplify her power against the Heavenly Principles and to open the Third Descender's seal. In 7.1 the Gnoses turned out to be remains of the Third Descender, Saarelainen.

Owners: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, then Nahida, then Dottore, and now the Tsaritsa. Canon never shows how it passed from Rukkhadevata to Nahida, her purest branch and next incarnation. The wiki treats them as the same object, which Dottore calls "the Gnosis of Sumeru".

Appearance: Like every Gnosis it is a gleaming, chess-piece-shaped object kept inside the Archon's chest. No in-game text describes its specific design.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): after 3.2, Nahida does not have it and the Akasha is not running. She treats the trade as a deal she chose, not a robbery, and few people outside her circle know about it. Do not return it to her.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-universe): a story object, never an inventory item. The Snezhnaya Awaits recap before 7.0 shows it beside Nahida's line about trading knowledge for the God of Wisdom's property.

139.comment: Dendro Gnosis: Dottore's bargain for the Dendro Gnosis
139.content:
In 3.2 Dottore (his Omega Build, segment 35) first traded Nahida the destruction of his other segments for the Electro Gnosis. Then he called the Gnosis "another chess piece" and asked for her Dendro Gnosis as a separate deal. Nahida called it arrogant, since people traditionally trade knowledge with the God of Wisdom, not for her property, but admitted she was interested. He told her the rumour that "the skies of Teyvat are fake", the secret Irminsul hides about the world's "truth", and she handed the Gnosis over.

In A Toast to Victory, Nahida says an important part of what she got "in return for my Gnosis" was the Fatui's record of the Descenders. By that record the Traveler is the Fourth Descender, and their twin is not counted as one. Her own hypothesis is that the First Descender was the Heavenly Principles. The Chinese text does not make clear whether she means the Dendro Gnosis, the Electro Gnosis or both.

140.comment: Dendro Gnosis: Akasha and the Dendro Gnosis
140.content: In her last memory, Rukkhadevata says she built the Akasha to compile people's wisdom, borrowing their dreams and joining all her own power to it. The Dendro Gnosis powered it. Only the Archon could run it at first; after her death the Akademiya sages took it over and stigmatised dreaming. Nahida shut it down in 3.2 after giving the Gnosis away.

141.comment: Dendro Gnosis: The Tsaritsa's six Gnoses
141.content: In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), the Tsaritsa placed her six Gnoses, the Dendro Gnosis among them, as energy nodes around a hall of Zapolyarny Palace. Her Cryo power, amplified by them, slowed time inside and stalled the Shade Rhinedottir. Rhinedottir called it power beyond what a god should have; the Tsaritsa credited her own insight as well.

key: The First Days of the City of Kings
142.content:
Desert Pavilion Chronicle (also: The First Days of the City of Kings, End of the Golden Realm, Timepiece of the Lost Path, Defender of the Enchanting Dream, Legacy of the Desert High-Born): Desert Pavilion Chronicle is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain). Its five item texts form one poem, recited by an old blind poet, about Gurabad: the shepherd Ormazd made vassal king with the Jinni Liloupar's help, his slide into tyranny, Liloupar's revenge, the city's fall, and the desert splintering into seven states.

Each piece addresses a different listener. The recurring warning is that love and power left unchecked destroy the city they build.

Lore: Legend says the Lord of the Sands, after his lover's death, made a pact with humanity through the Jinn: only incorruptible mortals could serve as vassal-kings. The Jinni Liloupar chose the shepherd Ormazd, warned him that her blessing carried "sharp retribution", and watched him ignore it. He united the clans, was crowned, and made Gurabad the mortals' capital.

Ormazd then took slaves, tribute and sacrifice and treated her advice as pillow talk, so Liloupar took off the earrings he had given her and swore three generations of ruin on his line.
