It was a reward of the Clink Clank Clash event in Nod-Krai. Its story takes place in the hidden court of the Seelie by Lake Amsvartnir, where a woman's lament recalls a dream and the last Seelie play a final tune.

Appearance: A catalyst: a lute with golden strings as radiant as sunlight, apparently a Seelie relic. Add no further detail.

Lore: Beyond the ruins of an ancient palace, at the edge of the Nod-Krai wasteland, stands the quiet sacred forest of Lake Amsvartnir. Legend says that whoever breaks the golden branch in the forest will find the royal court of the Seelie, hidden from mortal eyes by day.

The court is a kingdom of the past, forgotten by time and space and untouched by heavenly light. Its owner has long departed, leaving a neglected courtyard and a bare hall, yet a young woman's silent lament still echoes through the palace.

The lament says that the titan craftsman of the skies once wove the destinies of all living beings, with the golden harp as its instrument of fate, and that this was the heavens' divine plan. Yet even the ignorant can dream, and in her dream a new future appeared: men raising a tower to the heavens whose apostle wages war on the sky, roaring beasts larger than mountains breaking from the earth's bonds, and three moons shining on the sea before an ancient dragon rose like a tide and eclipsed them. Everything vanished when she woke, leaving only the memory of a glance from star-like eyes.

She wonders whether that was love or only delusion woven from hope, ambition and a longing for death, and says it no longer matters: their story has ended and became Elysium's finale. The text then likens insects chirping on a long-gone autumn night to a chorus of exiles singing mankind's oldest song, people who lost the place of their bodies and souls and keep only songs and memories of a homeland. The last singers, the first Seelie, played their final tune in the hall of angels. A wolf who once broke into the place has long gone, and only unfulfilled dreams remain, chasing phantoms. The text never explains who the dreaming woman is.

Owners: No owner is named. The Seelie are its implied makers or keepers, and the court's owner is described as long departed.

On the wiki the item text's "owner" of the court and "first Seelie" are linked to Koitar, but the item itself does not name that figure. Do not state who played the lute without a source.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10.0%; introduced in Version 6.0 as a reward from the Clink Clank Clash flagship event (2025-09-12 to 2025-09-29, requiring Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue archon quest), not from Wishes. Refinement uses Golden Strings rather than duplicate weapons, and four can be obtained in the event. Passive "Last Singer": for 20s after using an Elemental Skill, the wielder's Elemental Mastery increases by 100 (refinement 1) up to 200 (refinement 5).

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: treat it as a quiet Seelie-court legend from Nod-Krai, half-remembered and melancholy. Characters may know the golden-branch legend without knowing who the lamenting woman is, because the text leaves her unnamed. Mention that the weapon came from an event only when out-of-world context calls for it.

194.comment: Etherlight Spindlelute: The Royal Court of the Seelie
194.content: According to the Etherlight Spindlelute's story, the Seelie court by Lake Amsvartnir can be found by breaking the golden branch in the sacred forest, and is hidden from mortal eyes by day. Its owner has long departed. A woman's lament still echoes there, and the first Seelie played their last tune in its hall.

195.content:
Everlasting Moonglow (also: Fumetsu no Gekka, Byakuya Kougetsu, Pearl and waves catalyst): Everlasting Moonglow is a pearl-strung catalyst from the Sangonomiya and Watatsumi tradition. Its item text is a poetic history of Watatsumi Island: the people who dreamed with their god, the first Divine Priestess, the lightning that struck down their dream, and the memory that survives in the "pearl and waves" emblem.

It is a 5-star catalyst and, unusually, is not part of the Inazuma weapon series. Its description calls it a string of lovely jasper from the deep sea, shining with a pure radiance like the moon and "ever-distant".

Appearance: A string or ring of pearls and jewelled beads, with a pale moonlit glow, set with the Sangonomiya emblem. The description speaks of a string of lovely jasper from the deep sea; canon text says nothing more of its design.

Lore: The text begins with the "pearl and waves" emblem of the Sangonomiya, said to mean the waves that embrace Watatsumi and its bright pearls, though some say it shows the jewelled wheel of Watatsumi Omikami keeping eternal watch over the coral land like the moon. It then recalls how the descendants of their god passed hope from generation to generation.

The first Divine Priestess led her people with wisdom as precious as pearls and chose clergy from those newly introduced to sunlight, who comforted those who feared the day. The text also recalls the Umigozen, who made the navies of Narukami tremble and sang whale-songs with them, and says the emblem was drawn as they danced with the airborne kurage.

Later "a single bolt of lightning" rejected the Watatsumi people's dream, and the serpent slithered into the storm to face its glow. The children of the god and the pearl-hearted shrine maidens did not forget: tales, gratitude and the ring of ocean gems were passed down. The text lists what the emblem commemorates: the tearing of the jewelled branches, the birth of pearls, the defeat of the vishaps in the depths to bring sunlight to the pale nation beneath the waves, and the young man who dreamed of standing atop Mt. Yougou, was named an "evil king", and fought his great duel with the tengu. The final lines promise that even if storm clouds gather and the violet lightning is perilous, the silver moon of Watatsumi will still pierce through.

The "single bolt of lightning" is linked on the wiki to Musou no Hitotachi, the Raiden Shogun's stroke; Orobashi's entry holds the story of the serpent who faced it. The young man who dreamed of Mt. Yougou is Akuou, a figure from Inazuma's past; his own story belongs to his entry. The text reads as Watatsumi's version of events, favourable to its own people and critical of the lightning that ended their dream.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon. The weapon is tied to the Sangonomiya clan only by the emblem its text is built around.

Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess of Watatsumi, is the most natural in-world fit and is commonly equipped with it in play, but nothing in the item text says she owns it; if a scene needs an owner, make that a scene decision.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst released in Version 2.1 on the weapon event Wish. Base ATK 46 with HP% as secondary stat.

Its passive, Byakuya Kougetsu, raises the wielder's Healing Bonus (10% at refinement 1, 20% at refinement 5) and adds Normal Attack damage equal to a percentage of the wielder's Max HP (1% at refinement 1, 3% at refinement 5). For 12 seconds after an Elemental Burst, Normal Attacks that hit opponents restore 0.6 Energy, at most once every 0.1 seconds. Refinement increases the values. Ascension uses the Distant Sea branch materials of Watatsumi, prism boss drops and the Spectral line of enemy drops.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: use it as a Watatsumi heirloom-style catalyst, an object that carries a people's memory. Characters from Watatsumi may recognise the emblem; others may see only an elegant pearl charm. Avoid asserting that it is Kokomi's own.

196.comment: Everlasting Moonglow: Pearl and Waves Emblem
196.content: The "pearl and waves" emblem of the Sangonomiya clan is said to stand for the sea around Watatsumi and its pearls, though some say it shows the jewelled wheel of Watatsumi Omikami watching over the coral land like the moon. Everlasting Moonglow's text treats it as a symbol of memory that Watatsumi's people carry through loss.

197.content:
Exaiphanes Blade: The Exaiphanes Blade is a 5-star sword given to the Traveler during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (Chapter VII, Act I), described as a longsword that once shone with the light of the stars and in the voyager's hand becomes a new light unconnected to any past era. It reacts to Statues of The Seven in Snezhnaya and can only be strengthened at them. Added in Version 7.0.

Unlike other weapons it cannot be refined with ordinary materials. After the Traveler uses Cryo on a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya, the blade can be enhanced there once per Statue.

Appearance: Canon describes it as a longsword that once shone with the light of the stars, and in the Traveler's hand as a new light. No further detail is given in the cited text.

Lore: The blade is obtained in a special domain during Great Deeds on the Tundra, and it seems to react whenever the Traveler comes near a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya.

Each Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya can bless the sword once. The in-game Function Details say that the blade can only be enhanced at those Statues, after the Traveler uses Cryo to awaken and connect to them. The quest places the first enhancement at a Statue in Zolnyy.

Each enhancement stage has a short text. The first, Origin of Stellar Grace, speaks of a traveler who journeyed far into foreign lands for a slim chance of redemption. The second, Melody of the Astral Voices, says it is not known when the traveler gave up capturing sounds amid the eternal silence. The third, Boundless Journey to the Starry Sea, asks how long since someone looked at the stars hoping to find answers. The fourth, Solitary Drifting of the Astral Vessel, compares people to moths drawn to flame while an ordinary life still yearns to survive. The fifth, Grand Wish of the Shifting Stars, says darkness cannot dull the traveler's edge and that with swords and plowshares aboard a new beginning is within reach.

The wiki's table shows the blade's Level, ATK and CRIT Rate climbing with each Statue (for example ATK 122 after the first, 532 after the fourth, 608 after the fifth and sixth) with Refinement Rank rising to 4 at the sixth. The sixth stage is named Twilight of Fallen Stars; its description and the seventh stage were not filled in on the wiki. Treat the stage texts as item flavor: they do not say whom "the traveler" is.

Owners: The blade is the player's Traveler's weapon, obtained during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest. Its Traveler's Path passive applies only when the Traveler equips it.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a 5-star sword, base ATK 46, CRIT Rate secondary stat. The passive, Traveler's Path, grants CRIT DMG, ATK and Energy effects that scale with enhancement, can trigger even when the Traveler is off-field and has a cooldown. It needs no Mora or materials, and the Statue enhancement does not require the Traveler to be in the party. Obtained at step 18 of the quest, which grants the achievement Mystery Play of the Pale Star.

How {{char}} behaves: This archive's suggested use: a blade whose light belongs to the Traveler's own journey rather than any past age, strengthened by the Statues of The Seven in a frozen land. Do not explain its origin, because canon does not.

198.content: The Exaiphanes Blade is a 5-star sword obtained by the Traveler in the Version 7.0 Snezhnaya Archon Quest, a longsword once bright with starlight that becomes a new light in the Traveler's hand. It is enhanced only at Statues of The Seven in Snezhnaya after Cryo awakens them.

199.content:
Eye of Graeae (also: Graeae, Eye of Graeae gadget): The Eye of Graeae is a palm-sized mechanism that often takes the form of a monocle. The Traveler finds it in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, where it wakes, recognises them as a Descender, and agrees to serve them. In Snezhnaya it lets its user shape Prime Ice, protects against the killing cold by burning Kresnik Energy, calls a train, and speaks as a polite, forgetful voice that is trying to recover its lost power.

It carries a fragmentary mind that was made, by its own account, within the Hvergelmir project. Over the Snezhnaya story it moves from a helpful gadget to a character with its own mission, and the story ends with the device keeping its functions but losing that voice.

Appearance: In the inventory it is a quick-use gadget, described as a strange mechanism from an abandoned station that "often appears in the form of a monocle" and seems to have many convenient functions. On the Traveler's train it also sits on a pedestal at the front of the carriage, where it is used to set a destination.

Its readouts appear on the HUD as an orange Kresnik Energy bar above the active character's health bar. The gadget screen also shows the character's stats and current firearm loadout.

Lore: The Eye was left in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, untouched through the cataclysm. When it wakes, its memories are broken and its power is scattered across the tundra. It senses the pieces in three places and asks the Traveler for help, as the one it has "signed a contract to serve".

Its message log is also a window onto Snezhnaya. It explains the four cold zones (normal, low, frigid and subzero), which Kresnik's Torches created by warming parts of a land that was once only frigid and subzero. It tells how trains were first conceived for the needs of Hvergelmir's Shadow Realm exploration, and that the technology became public after the Tsaritsa took the throne. It explains that the Shadow Realm firearms were designed for fighting where living beings cannot use elemental power, and that Hvergelmir researchers modelled them on Hyperborean energy-storage devices.

Its own account in the Pale Crown Palace quest is that Aksinya and Hvergelmir made it, and that it was divided into three segments before the cataclysm to create the first "prototype human", with the aim of bringing humanity to "Tomorrow". It realised that if the pieces fused and gained the authority of the Primordial Human, this would threaten humans and fae. It asked to be divided and persuaded Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to stop Aksinya finishing the experiment. They did, for their own reasons, and Aksinya was cast into the Shadow Realm.

The Traveler recovers the three fragments from the House of Hesperides, Flamefeather Valley and the Pale Crown Palace. Aksinya takes the restored Eye in the Court of Eternal Bliss, and the Primordial Human is awakened. At the end the Eye asks the Traveler what they would do if their sibling became a different person. The Traveler says they would learn to love who that person became. The Eye asks to be stopped along with Aksinya, and both fall into the Shadow Realm.

The Eye's messages add commentary on the people tied to its fragments: it says Pavlina was a major Hvergelmir researcher whose Prime Ice work built cold laboratories and preserved Hyperborean finds, and it doubts it can be certain whether Aksinya created it. About the Flamefeather Valley rite, it says it feels it has seen the relief before. Of Koshchei it says he turned his life into a near-eternal form because its fragment alone could not carry his full transcendence, and it sounds sorry for him. These are the Eye's own reconstructions, not neutral history.

Owners: The Traveler carries the Eye as a standard gadget. Paimon is present for most of its story and helps them search for its power. Aksinya takes the restored Eye in the Court of Eternal Bliss.

Gameplay: Gameplay description, not story. The gadget works only in Snezhnaya.
- Fab-Vision harvests Prime Ice and builds or removes Prime Ice Constructs in the open world, usable while running, falling and in combat but not while gliding or swimming.
- It stores Kresnik Energy (up to 100%) and Prime Ice Resource (up to 400). Both are spent building constructs; Kresnik Energy is also drained to prevent cold damage, and drains quickly in frigid and subzero zones.
- It calls the Traveler's train near any railway track.
- It shows the character's stats and firearm loadout for the Shadow Realm third-person shooter mode.
- It keeps the message log and a Prime Ice Construct archive.

key: Messages from the Eye of Graeae
200.comment: Eye of Graeae: Eye of Graeae Messages
200.content: The message feature unlocks after the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands". New texts arrive as "a new message from the Eye of Graeae" and cover quest background and exploration tips. Examples are the cold zones, the train and its history, the Shadow Realm firearms, Snegovik and Aksinya. Most appear only after specific quests. The Eye says its information comes from a database fed by an uploader named Hvergelmir, which it suspects is not a real name.

201.comment: Eye of Graeae: Fab-Vision and Kresnik Energy
201.content: Fab-Vision is the gadget's construction mode: tap to harvest Prime Ice or build and remove constructs from blueprints. Constructing needs Kresnik Energy and Prime Ice Resource. Kresnik Energy also guards against the cold and runs out fast in the harshest zones. The Eye once noted unusual energy fluctuations when constructs are condensed, and speculated, flagged as speculation, that condensing gives form to a possibility that also exists in many other worlds.

202.content:
Fables de Fontaine (also: Fables of Fontaine, Fontaine Animal Fables): The three tales are "The Maiden and the Sun", "The Crow and the Fox" and "The Tale of the Donkey". All are moral fables with talking animals. Vol. 3 follows directly from Vol. 2, since the donkey tries to copy the fox's trick.

Appearance: A 4-star book collection of three volumes. Vol. 1 is sold by Hubel in the Court of Fontaine (Quartier Narbonnais). Vol. 2 lies at Romaritime Harbor next to Hermosa. Vol. 3 lies in front of the Beaumont Workshop. The cover title is written in the Fontaine Script.

Lore: Vol. 2, "The Crow and the Fox": a crow on a tree holds stolen cheese. The fox below first warns that the cheese is dangerous, then that it is no delicacy, then claims the crow does not know how to eat it properly and that she has collected recipes from around the world. Curious, the crow opens its beak to ask, drops the cheese, and the fox takes it and runs to her nest. The moral is that those who seek mysteries they should not know will lose even what they had.

Vol. 3, "The Tale of the Donkey": after hearing how the fox won the cheese, a donkey resents that others praise the fox and ignore its own hard work. It copies her, ambushes a cheesemaker's daughter and tells her to throw her cheese away to travel faster. She takes it for mockery, calls for a stick and threatens to drive it back to the mill, and the donkey falls silent. The moral is that imitating someone else and hiding your own identity brings only more suffering.

Vol. 3 opens with its own framing remarks before the story: that a plain person dressed up is rarely mistaken for a socialite, and that everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses, so the way forward is to know oneself and face one's flaws. In Vol. 2 the fox says the cheesemakers of the city let the crow keep the cheese, and in Vol. 3 the donkey's victim is a cheesemaker's daughter, which links the last two volumes. The fox's argument in Vol. 2 is a string of misleading claims, yet the stated moral blames the crow's curiosity rather than the fox's deceit.

Placement notes: the three fables are physically separated, with one volume at each of three Fontaine locations, so a reader needs to visit the Court of Fontaine, Romaritime Harbor and the Beaumont Workshop to hold the whole set. The in-game description frames the collection as folklore compiled under one author's name, so a character may cite it as a popular storybook but should not claim the tales are historical.

Owners: No owner. It is a commercial book collection scattered across Fontaine.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 4-star Book Collection added in 4.0. The wiki notes that the real-world models are fables by Jean de La Fontaine (the first tale resembles "The Mouse Turned into a Maid", the second "The Fox and the Crow"). The Fontaine-Script cover reads "les fables".

203.comment: Fables de Fontaine: Fox in Fables de Fontaine
203.content: In Fables de Fontaine the fox is a clever, deceitful figure: she is mother to the maiden who weds the sun in Vol. 1 and cheats the crow of its cheese in Vol. 2. The donkey of Vol. 3 fails to copy her. These are unnamed fictional animals with no known canon counterpart.

204.content:
Fang of the Mountain King (also: Turquoise Hunt, Kongamato's fang): Fang of the Mountain King is a 5-star claymore, a giant sword forged from pure turquoise. It is named for Kongamato, the Mountain King, because it is far heavier than ordinary weapons.

The item text is less about the blade than about the beast: a Yumkasaur who once protected the tribes and now guards a fire it no longer remembers.

Appearance: A giant sword of pure turquoise, heavier than ordinary weapons. Canon adds nothing about its shape; keep descriptions to a massive blue-green claymore.

Lore: In the heart of Huitztlan sleeps Kongamato, the Mountain King, a creature as vast as the mountains around it. In its half-waking, searing pain it treats everything that approaches as a mortal enemy and attacks without distinction.

Tribespeople say it once protected them and was driven mad by the dark disaster of the Cataclysm, yet no one can explain why it only attacks what comes near.

Its sanity was lost long ago, when its fangs pierced the flesh of Burkina (the wiki names him as its human companion). Legends speak of the person who made pacts with it and hunted at its side, but those memories are gone in the Mountain King's long nightmare, and even the name Kongamato is unfamiliar to the ancient lord of the Yumkasaurs.

Yet it must at least protect the fire, though it knows not whose it is. Its body, once its pride, is wracked by burning agony and bears the marks of unbearable shame, and its soul has been consumed by the filth of darkness. The text says it will not abandon this last shred of resolve.

The poem ends with three lines in a speaker's voice: that the Turnfire name will be returned to the Night Realm in exchange for the final kindling, that life marches on by past fuel and present flame, and that all will answer to the fire for their deeds and be reunited in the flames. In the wiki's account of Kinich's story, the Scions of the Canopy periodically drain Kongamato's Abyssal energy in the Turnfire Ritual; during one such ritual it begged to be put out of its misery, and was told by Kinich that it must live with its shame. That fits the item's themes of guilt and duty, but the item text does not mention Kinich.

Owners: No wielder is named. The sword is named after Kongamato rather than owned by anyone.

The only person tied to the legend is Burkina, the former partner of the Mountain King. Do not give the sword to a character without making it a scene invention.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star claymore, base ATK 49 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT Rate; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.0.

Passive "Turquoise Hunt": hitting an opponent with an Elemental Skill grants a stack of Canopy's Favor (once per 0.5s). When a nearby party member triggers Burning or Burgeon, the wielder gains 3 stacks (once per 2s, even if the trigger is off-field). Each stack raises Elemental Skill and Burst DMG by 10% at refinement 1 up to 20% at refinement 5, for 6s, to a maximum of 6 stacks counted independently. Ascension uses Sacred Lord Delirious materials, the Ignited boss materials and whistle common materials.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: a Scions of the Canopy speaker would treat the Mountain King with sorrow and respect, not as a mere monster. Avoid giving the sword a manufacturing story; canon only says it is turquoise and named for him.

205.comment: Fang of the Mountain King: Turquoise Hunt
205.content: Turquoise Hunt is the passive of the claymore Fang of the Mountain King (gameplay): it builds stacks of Canopy's Favor to raise Elemental Skill and Burst damage, with extra stacks from nearby Burning or Burgeon reactions.

206.comment: Fang of the Mountain King: Kongamato
206.content: Kongamato, the Mountain King, is a gigantic Yumkasaur of Huitztlan, archived as the Gluttonous Yumkasaur Mountain King. It has lived since the Cataclysm, fought the Abyss at the side of its human companion Burkina, and was severely afflicted by Abyssal energy, part of which the Scions of the Canopy drain in their Turnfire Ritual. It roused when its territory was disturbed and appears in a world-boss fight; in the wiki's account it resonates with Kinich as an heir to the Turnfire.

207.content:
Favonius Codex: Favonius Codex is a 4-star catalyst, a secret tome that belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius. It records the logic and power of elements and matter and is inlaid with crystallized elements. Every copy is hand-made, and its text is partly about the order's great library.

It is the one non-standard-issue weapon of the Favonius series, which otherwise holds the knights' swords, spear and bow.

Appearance: A tome set with crystallized elements. The wiki notes that the Teyvat script on the inside reads "Zephyrus", the Greek counterpart of the Roman Favonius.

Lore: The book holds the collective knowledge of the Knights' scholars. Its crystals are precious both in themselves and because each codex is made by hand; the text says only scholars who truly understand the workings of the elements can make such crystals.

When the Knights of Favonius were founded, the Dawn Knight Ragnvindr turned the aristocrats' indoor baths into a library. Contributions from bards, scholars and travelers made it the largest collection of writing in the northern half of the continent. The text reasons that songs are carried off by the wind and wine's pleasure is brief, but what is written down may shine for ever.

The collection is now a fraction of its peak size (the Chinese text gives one sixth) because the library once burned in the "Great Fire of Fall Equinox". In the library basement stands a sturdy poplar-wood door said to predate the library and to have withstood the smoke and flames. The text adds that the door stood there long before the Knights of Favonius existed. The Knights officially say the restricted section lies behind it, but tales hint at something more profound hidden within.

The wiki links the hidden secret to the Imaginarium Theater, but the text itself stops at the hint. In a scene, keep the poplar door as rumor and the Knights' official line, and do not decide what is behind it.

Owners: No owner is named. The text says it belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius.

The wiki notes the ascended codex is seen with Sucrose in her character card, Mona in her demo and Lisa in a 4-panel comic; this is art, not an ownership claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star catalyst, base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10.0%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

The passive needs a CRIT hit that deals damage, and in co-op the particles go to all team members.

208.content: Windfall is the shared passive of the Favonius series (gameplay). It lets CRIT hits occasionally create Elemental Particles that restore Energy.

209.content: The Knights of Favonius' library was begun by Ragnvindr in the former aristocrats' baths, grew into the largest collection in the northern half of the continent, and was later reduced by a fire called the Great Fire of Fall Equinox. A poplar-wood door older than the Knights stands in its basement.

210.content:
Favonius Greatsword: Favonius Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Favonius series, a heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive, and its text tells of the Lion of Light Arundolyn and his childhood friend Rostam the Wolf Pup.

It is usually issued only after approval from both the Grand Master and the Church.

Appearance: A heavy, ceremonial greatsword. The wiki's trivia remarks that the crossguard and pommel resemble a famous fantasy-film sword; this is a design observation, not canon.

Lore: The text calls it an honor given to a Knight of Favonius and the fruit of the work and skills of Mondstadt's craftsmen, who achieved results in elemental affinity by studying the city's ancient artifacts. It reminds the bearer that destruction is only a means; the end is to defend what must be defended.

Only a single-handed form of Rostam's Favonius Bladework survives today. Another form is lost to history: that of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, who could wield a longsword and a greatsword together in battle. It demanded such strength that only the extraordinarily gifted could try it, and it died out.

Arundolyn came from a long line of knights and Rostam from a peasant family. They were close companions growing up, with a shared dream of heroism, became fellow knights as young men, and as mature adults one became Grand Master and the other his assistant. Arundolyn was no Vision bearer; his formidable strength came from natural gifts and intense training, and it was his pride and the pride of the Knights and all Mondstadt.

After Rostam met his fate, Arundolyn never displayed that strength again, because challenging ferocious monsters no longer brought glory. For fuller detail on either man, defer to their own entries.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

The wiki notes the sword is shown with Noelle in her art, Hangout quest endings and Travelers' Tales, and with Diluc in several quests and videos; this is art, not an ownership claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

211.content: Windfall is the shared passive of the Favonius series (gameplay). It lets CRIT hits occasionally create Elemental Particles that restore Energy.

212.content: Favonius Bladework originated with Rostam, the Wolf Pup. Per the Favonius Greatsword text, only a single-handed form survives, because the dual longsword-and-greatsword form of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, required extraordinary strength and died out.

213.content:
Favonius Lance: Favonius Lance is a 4-star polearm of the Favonius series, a spear of honor among the Knights of Favonius. It is used in parades and reviews yet is also a keen foe of monsters. Its text recounts how spears came to Mondstadt and how the noble Eberhart took one up.

The shaft is straight and the tip flows lightly like the wind. It is the weapon that tells of spear use in Mondstadt, from commoners' stakes to a noble's secret training.

Appearance: A polearm in the Knights of Favonius' style: a straight shaft and a tip described as flowing lightly like the wind.

Lore: The text calls it a crystallization of the work and artistry of Mondstadt's defenders. By studying the arbor that held firm in the wind, the city's craftsmen and scholars learned much about elemental affinities. In hand, it reminds the Knights to be disciplined and to defend Mondstadt's freedom.

Polearms of a kind have long been the weapon of those who lack martial training: even untrained commoners with sharpened wooden sticks might match trained soldiers' steel. To celebrate the overthrow of the aristocracy, long stakes, flagpoles and pitchforks were stuck all over the greenery around the city. Nobles were once required to study the sword, and the spear was left to foreign gladiators and traitors.

One noble scion nonetheless wielded a spear: Eberhart, said to enjoy the night breeze while catching the first dew on his spear tip. An illegitimate child, he dreamed of recapturing the glory of ancient nobility and needed power to destroy its rotten foundations. The text offers two possible routes: inciting his legitimate brother to pursue a phantom thief's dream and then deceiving him into fleeing so that he could take the legitimacy, or pledging himself to a spear-wielding witch as a disciple to learn the fatal loophole in her art in order to slay her. The brother is linked by the wiki to Parsifal.

The entry ends on Eberhart's own defiant line that he will do anything for his goals even if later generations despise him. In a scene, present the two routes as alternatives, as the text does, and attribute any firm claim to the wiki's reading rather than the item.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

The wiki notes Mika is shown with the unascended lance in his character demo; this is art, not an ownership claim.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star polearm, base ATK 44, secondary stat Energy Recharge 6.7%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

214.content: Windfall is the shared passive of the Favonius series (gameplay). It lets CRIT hits occasionally create Elemental Particles that restore Energy.

215.content: Eberhart was the one noble known to wield a spear in the aristocratic age, an illegitimate child who dreamed of restoring ancient nobility. The Favonius Lance text leaves open whether he betrayed his legitimate brother, trained under a spear-witch in order to kill her, or both.

216.content:
Favonius Sword: Favonius Sword is a 4-star sword of the Favonius series, the standard-issue longsword of the Knights of Favonius. Its text credits Favonius Bladework to Rostam the Wolf Pup, childhood friend of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, and says Rostam's skill has never been matched.

It is usually issued after approval of both the Master of the order and the Church. The Version 6.4 story quest for Varka features a Favonius Sword that speaks in Rostam's name.

Appearance: A light, agile longsword of the Knights of Favonius. Jean is shown with the ascended version in most official artwork, her manga, her TCG card and her Collected Miscellany, per the wiki.

Lore: Mondstadt's craftsmen studied Mondstadt's Anemo to reach elemental affinity, and the sword is both an honor to a knight and the fruit of the defenders' skill. The text warns that its sharp blade is for defending, not attacking.

Favonius Bladework began with Rostam, the childhood friend and spiritual counterpart of Arundolyn. The legend says he could cut every raindrop out of the sky and that the wind from his sword dance could split a rose and put out a torch. The style is light, swift and precise in the defense of Mondstadt.

At twenty-seven, Rostam received the title of Wolf Pup. The Knights' tradition reserved the titles of Lion and Wolf for those with the leadership potential to become Grand Master someday. He served faithfully but did not live to see that day. No other practitioner has matched his legendary ability since, but his fervor and will to protect Mondstadt have stayed with the knights.

Version 6.4 detail: in Lonely Warrior, a part of Varka's Lupus Majoris Chapter, Varka comes upon a Favonius Sword and asks who left it there. The sword speaks, wishing aloud to be taken to see someone, and grants him a wind blessing called Rostam's Longing. The wiki labels the voice as Rostam's. Treat it as an echo of him in the setting, not as proof of a spirit.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Jean is the character most often shown with it, per the wiki; this is art, not a statement in the item text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star sword, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

217.content: Windfall is the shared passive of the Favonius series (gameplay). It lets CRIT hits occasionally create Elemental Particles that restore Energy.

218.content: In the Version 6.4 Varka story quest Lonely Warrior, a Favonius Sword grants Varka a wind blessing named Rostam's Longing, which in the quest gives him a cooldown-reduction buff (gameplay) and later forms a shield against a gale. The wiki labels the sword's voice as Rostam.

219.content:
Favonius Warbow: Favonius Warbow is a 4-star bow of the Favonius series, a recurve bow issued only to the Knights of Favonius' best, long-serving archers. Its text tells of the Outriders, the Knights' archer scouts, and how the team declined after their first member left.

It can be obtained as a reward for the A Long Shot quest and from Wishes.

Appearance: An oak-framed recurve bow with metal parts that make it easy to use. The bowstring is described as enchanted with the secrets of alchemy and magic, protecting the archer's fingers.

Lore: The bow is a reward for worthy guardians of Mondstadt and a tool for their continued guardianship. The text says the Knights once had a formidable team of archer scouts called the Outriders, founded by a mercenary leader from Liyue who passed on a lifetime of knowledge.

The Outriders gained tracking skills and a sense for approaching danger that were unique among the Knights and invaluable to the order. This lasted until the first of the Outriders left the order for reasons unknown to the Knights.

After that departure, the team became a shell of its former self: its expertise was gone, though its structure and name were kept. The text ends by noting that there are still those who work tirelessly to maintain the dignity of the Outrider title; the wiki links that line to Amber.

In a scene, keep the Outriders' decline as the item states it. Do not name the founder or the departed member unless the user supplies a name.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star bow, base ATK 41, secondary stat Energy Recharge 13.3%, obtainable from Wishes including the standard banner and as a reward for the Archon quest A Long Shot. Passive Windfall: CRIT hits have a chance (60% to 100% by refinement) to generate a small amount of Elemental Particles, restoring 6 Energy, once per 12 s at refinement 1 down to once per 6 s at refinement 5.

220.content: Windfall is the shared passive of the Favonius series (gameplay). It lets CRIT hits occasionally create Elemental Particles that restore Energy.

221.content: The Outriders are the Knights of Favonius' archer scouts, once founded by a Liyue mercenary leader. After the first of them left for unknown reasons, only the structure and name remained. The Favonius Warbow text says some still work to maintain the dignity of the title.

222.content:
Festering Desire (also: Undying Admiration, Durin's sword): Festering Desire is a creepy straight sword that almost seems to yearn for life, dripping with a shrivelling venom that could corrupt even a mighty dragon. Its blade was coated with powder made of the dragon Durin's remains. The Traveler received it as a memento from Albedo after the 1.2 event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon, once the corruption had been drawn out.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a creepy straight sword that seems to yearn for life and drips with a shrivelling venom. No other visual detail is given in text.

Lore: The item text recalls a memory of the dragon Durin, as a child of Rhinedottir. Rhinedottir's words speak of unborn life and unfulfilled wishes at the edge of the universal darkness, asking them to dwell in her body and descend into the world, then go to a lovely place and show their own beauty. Durin answers: "Thank you, Mother, thank you." He says she gave him wings and a mighty form, and that he wishes to go to a land of lovely songs and tell them the place he was born is beautiful.

Albedo explains the sword's history in the event quest Festering Desire. A blacksmith made it and vanished soon after. The blade was lost to time and ended up with Treasure Hoarders, from whom the Knights of Favonius recovered it with other stolen goods. As nobody claimed it, Albedo studied it and found that the blade had been coated with a powder of Durin's remains, especially his eyes, claws and scales. That gave it Durin's power and also his corruption, so ordinary mortals could not use it, since the corruption might seep through the handle into the wielder.

Albedo considers the sword almost a living being and wonders if the curse was why its maker disappeared. The Traveler was unaffected because they can purify abyssal corruption, as they had done with Dvalin's tears, so Albedo gave them the sword to experiment on. The Traveler purified it over time in the story ending with Raiders Amidst Snow Mist, though some of its power was accidentally transferred into the Resurgent Cryo Regisvine in Uninvited Guests. In the Afterword Albedo extracted what remained of the corruption into a bottle and gave the now safe sword to the Traveler as a keepsake of their research.

Owners: No lasting owner except the Traveler, who receives it from Albedo as a memento. Before that it passed from its unnamed maker to Treasure Hoarders and then into Knights of Favonius custody.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star sword obtained from the event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon. Base ATK 42, secondary stat Energy Recharge 10%. Passive "Undying Admiration": raises Elemental Skill DMG and Elemental Skill CRIT Rate (16-32% and 6-12% at refinement 1-5). During the event it also gave Dragonspine boosts.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the sword suits scenes about inherited harm and the line between study and obsession. Albedo handles it with clinical care; do not have ordinary mortals wield it uncorrupted. By 7.1 canon the corruption in the sword itself is gone.

223.content: The wiki notes that Festering Desire's lore ties into the Dragonspine Spear, since both weapons are made from the remains of Durin. The shared origin is established by weapon text; the Dragonspine Spear has its own entry.

key: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
224.comment: Festering Desire: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
224.content: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon was a limited-time event (version 1.2, Dragonspine) in which Albedo investigates this sword with the Traveler. It gave the sword as a reward and, while it ran, granted bonuses in Dragonspine when the sword was used there.

225.content:
Finale of the Deep: Finale of the Deep is a four-star sword of the Beaumont series, made by forging in Fontaine. Its description calls the longsword as silent as the ocean depths and older than its styling suggests. The item story says it once belonged to a musician whose name is forgotten, a proud figure of Remuria's golden era whose doctrine of music as authority ended in catastrophe.

The sword is covered in ostentatious decoration and gems, which the text takes as proof that its owner was no ordinary instrumentalist. Lynette is shown wielding it in the Version 4.0 trailer and other promotional material.

Appearance: A ceremonial longsword with layer upon layer of decoration and shining gems. When wielded by a character who has Arkhe, the teardrop-shaped gem on the hilt glows with Pneuma or Ousia.

The wiki lists the base and second-ascension looks as separate models. Lynette carries the ascended version in the 4.0 trailer, her character demo and her Collected Miscellany, and the unascended one in the Into the Sunlight event.

Lore: Legend holds that the sword belonged to a musician, now nameless, who was fiercely proud of an ancient grand symphony he never performed for anyone, believing that no age of chaos would answer it with applause or lament, and that no one would transcribe so complex a work. An opera in Fontaine portrays his life: nobody knows his origins, but everyone understands his tragedy. Like many of humble birth, he decided his fate in the city to which all waterways lead.

In the text he teaches at a towering theater academy, telling students that musicians must be like those who transcend, voicing the sublime with passion so that glory follows passion, unity follows glory and order follows unity. He casts music as the scepter and shield of authority and holds that the passion of vanquishing foes and loving comrades divides humanity into masters and slaves. This understanding raised him to the loftiest of halls, and in Remuria's golden era listeners were intoxicated by it.

The story ends when a mountainous wave destroys the academy. In the wreckage, the skeletal remains of people burned away by the musician's passion are exposed beneath the foundations. The text thus presents the sublime he preached as having been built on those who were consumed by it. The item text does not say who the musician was; the wiki links the places named (the Collegium Phonascorum, the Domus Aurea, Remuria) to the setting.

Owners: The nameless musician of legend is the only former owner named in the text. In the current game it is associated with Lynette through trailer and promotional appearances.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive An End Sublime: using an Elemental Skill grants a percentage ATK increase for 15 seconds and a Bond of Life worth 25% of Max HP (once per 10 seconds). Clearing the Bond of Life gives extra flat ATK based on the amount cleared, for 15 seconds, and only if the Bond was increased by this weapon at some point. Base ATK is 44 with ATK 6% as its secondary stat.

226.content:
Finale of the Deep Galleries (also: Deep Gallery's Echoing Song, Deep Gallery's Distant Pact, Deep Gallery's Moment of Oblivion, Deep Gallery's Bestowed Banquet, Deep Gallery's Lost Crown): Finale of the Deep Galleries is a 4- and 5-star Cryo artifact set. Its five Deep Gallery pieces carry item text about Skirk, following her master Surtalogi's guidance, walking the frozen north to find relics, with each piece telling part of a legend of the first angel, a stranger from beyond the stars and the Golden City's fall. Mechanically it rewards a character at zero Energy.

The text interleaves two layers: a short frame in which "the girl" (Skirk) searches northern ruins, and a long past in which a youth and the first angel rebel against the heavens. The pieces were released in version 5.5.

Appearance: All pieces are made of northland jade: an icy flower whose petals crumbled, a shimmering feathered accessory, a pocket watch frozen at its moment of destruction, a ceremonial cup, and a helmet with jade ornamentation from an older age. Per the wiki Skirk wears a feather resembling the Distant Pact in her hair.

Lore: Every piece begins with the girl's trek: following her master, she crosses the freezing wastelands and the corridor of fractured mirrors and kills monsters in the ruins before finding a treasure under snow beside a silver tree, Abyssal remnants, the golden tower, the Spiral Abyss ruins or a tattered veil. The legend:
Across the five pieces: a youth asks the first angel about forbidden origins, she breaks her bonds and loves him, the Golden City forges fae and dreams of a world without tears, the heavens destroy it with crystal spikes, and her kin are cursed so that an angel who loves one alone ends as a Seelie.

Piece by piece:
- Echoing Song: a youth who ventured deep underground asked the first angel about the world's most forbidden origins. She was shaken but he revealed his own origin, and the fetters of the enthroned ruler broke for her; she told him the secret of creation. He swore to be her sword, shield and conspirator, and she kissed his forehead. The heavenly moons saw.
- Distant Pact: before the Frostmoon Scions' dream, a voyager (a scribe duty-bound not to commune with primordial civilisations) was drawn by a light from a small world and its primeval dragon. She offered the dragon-lord escape from a doomed world; he refused, calling his people the meaning of the universe and choosing to be their bulwark. When she returned the dragon was gone, the earth bound under four shackles and light split into seven hues; she placed her mind in a youth's body in the city of gold.
- Moment of Oblivion: the Golden City's furnaces forged fae spirits on giant bones with frostmoon light, a creative authority the rebellious envoy gave to mortals in hope of a perfect being. The first angel dreamed of a future with no tears or death. Blue crystal spikes fell, the fae became silver mist, and the envoy was stripped of name and form with a curse on her kin: love given to one alone would crumble beauty and mind until a Seelie rose from the remains.
- Bestowed Banquet: the priests of the Golden City blamed one another for the angels' wrath. A boy of humble birth slipped in and refuted them; the chief priest told him to drink the cup of wrath and take his case to the envoys at the ashen-silver tree.
- Lost Crown: angels, silver-winged, crowned with sevenfold radiance, were loyal servants of the sky until the first angel met the youth, loved him freely and cast her star-crown into the snow, vowing to build a city and tower so humans need weep no more.
The Seelie origin is the notable canon claim: it presents the Seelie as the remains of fallen angels cursed for singling out one beloved. The wiki notes overlap with Records of Jueyun Vol. 4 on an angel and a traveller from beyond Teyvat. The Golden City is tied by wiki links to Hyperborea; the curse and the crown scene are told from a loving-rebel perspective, not a neutral historian's.

The text keeps its voice strictly separate from Skirk's own knowledge: it never says what she learned, only that she found the objects. Names are withheld, so linking the youth/voyager to Anacharsis and the dragon-lord to the Nibelung is wiki-link inference (see uncertainties). The Distant Pact's mention of the Frostmoon Scions' "sweet dream of submergence" and the Echoing Song's mention of the war of funerary flame place the narrator in a later age than the events.

Owners: No owner is named. The text implies Skirk finds the relics; otherwise they are described as lost objects of an ancient civilisation.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): 4- and 5-star; domain Derelict Masonry Dock in Natlan (5.5) and an Artifact Strongbox. 4-piece: while the wearer has 0 Elemental Energy, Normal Attack DMG +60% and Burst DMG +60%. Dealing Normal Attack DMG pauses the Burst bonus for 6s, and dealing Burst DMG pauses the Normal Attack bonus for 6s. It can trigger off-field.

227.comment: Finale of the Deep Galleries: Finale of the Deep Galleries
227.content: Artifact set whose item text is set during Skirk's northward search and recounts the first angel, a stranger from the stars and the Golden City.

228.comment: Finale of the Deep Galleries: The first angel's curse
228.content: In the Moment of Oblivion text the traitorous envoy is stripped of name and form after the Golden City falls. Her kin are cursed: any angel who singles out one beloved will lose divine beauty and mind until a Seelie rises from the remains, drifting to consume fading memories.

229.content:
Flame-Forged Insight (also: Mind in Bloom): Flame-Forged Insight is a 4-star claymore from Natlan. The People of the Springs are said to have forged a great blade to protect a child who would go on a distant journey, and this weapon is a replica of that legendary sword.

Its story is told through two old adventurers, Akamai and Kau Kau, who melted down the stones of a lifetime of travel to arm a descendant. It was an event reward in Version 5.8.

Appearance: Canon gives only the description of a replica of a legendary great blade. Do not invent engravings. The story only notes that it was forged from crystal and ore gathered on the old friends' travels.

Lore: Akamai and Kau Kau, two youths of the People of the Springs, once swore to explore all of Natlan and see their deeds recorded on woven scrolls. Their treasures turned out to be mostly ordinary ore and crystals, but they treasured them anyway.

Each stone held a memory: one taken from beneath the claws of a giant Tepetlisaurus in crystal mountains, one from the fiend that tripped them by a hot spring when they were drunk, one ash-covered stone that had kept watch on the edge of the burned ancient city of Ochkanatlan before they took it.

When Akamai's descendant wanted to follow a forebear's path, now-aged Akamai and Kau Kau (one walking with a cane) had the blacksmith from the mountains melt the stones down and forge a blade to protect the traveller. They handed it over as a parting gift, saying the past accompanies the young in place of ancestors who no longer have the strength, and that the past flows through the blood like a fire passed down by rituals that never stop burning.

The story is told as inherited tribal tradition, with dialogue for the old friends. The reforging motif is stated in the story itself: as the smith melts each stone, the past stirs again with each memory spoken, and the closing lines liken the past flowing through the blood to a fire passed down by never-ending rituals.

Owners: No owner is named. The wiki calls this particular weapon a replica of the legendary sword.

Within the story the blade passes from Akamai and Kau Kau to Akamai's unnamed descendant. Any scene claiming the original still exists is an invention.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star claymore of the Meztli series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat Elemental Mastery. Reward of the Version 5.8 event Sunspray Summer Resort; refinement material is Drifter's Crystal Marrow.

Passive "Mind in Bloom": when Electro-Charged, Lunar-Charged, Bloom, Lunar-Bloom, Crystallize or Lunar-Crystallize is triggered, restores Elemental Energy and raises Elemental Mastery for 15s, once per 15s, even when the wielder is off-field.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: a keepsake-weapon with a sentimental legend. Natlanese elders may tell it as a story about friends, journeys and passing the past to the young.

230.content: Mind in Bloom is the passive of the claymore Flame-Forged Insight (gameplay): it triggers on several reactions (Electro-Charged, Bloom, Crystallize and their Lunar versions), restoring Energy and raising Elemental Mastery for a while, even off-field.

231.content:
Fleuve Cendre Ferryman (also: the Ferryman): Fleuve Cendre Ferryman is a four-star sword from Fontaine that is, plainly, a handy length of abandoned copper pipe once used as a weapon, famous or infamous depending on the circle. Its item story belongs to Eduardo Baker, an outlaw leader of the Fleuve Cendre, who called it the Ferryman for the many who went into the grey river with it. It is obtained from the Fontaine Fishing Association rather than forged.

The story ends with a photograph of Eduardo and others taken in Poisson during a hostage incident, which the Marechaussee Hunters resolved.

Appearance: A discarded copper (the text also says bronze) pipe, kept like a cane in the photograph in which Eduardo leans on it.

Lore: The text says discarded components in the gutters can serve as a weapon in an emergency. This pipe's first opponent was a monster nourished by 'richly nutritious water', and it broke the knees and jaws of countless 'livestock' who threatened Eduardo's countrymen. The Court of Fontaine's bureaucracy could not keep order in the Fleuve Cendre, so the outlaw leader began his rise by beating back crocodiles with it, protecting merchants from gangs, settling disputes and blessing newlyweds, until it was said that the sun's light belonged to them and the Fleuve Cendre to 'us'.

The story then turns to the city's drive for improvement, in which people could not be moved but their coordinates could, and the distinction between 'them' and 'us' became merely places to develop and trash to dispose of or 'move'. Eduardo was arrested in the purge of the Fleuve Cendre and was being taken to exile in the desert when his henchmen rescued him. With comrades near Mont Automnequi, they occupied Poisson, seized members of the Maison Gardiennage who were transporting them as hostages and made a series of unreasonable demands. The Marechaussee Hunters ended the incident.

The reporter Karl Ingold volunteered to deliver the demands and took a photograph in Poisson before things worsened. In it Eduardo rests his free hand on his son Jakob's shoulder, Jakob clutching the sleeve of Rene de Petrichor; the Great Magician Parsifal leans casually on the railing; Poisson's mayor Renault de Petrichor stands formally dressed, collar askew; and Rosa Reed with her infant, her husband Thompson and Tom Alter stand at the far end. The text says they all look ahead, 'on the future'.

Owners: Eduardo Baker, whose hands gave it the nickname Ferryman.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive Ironbone raises CRIT Rate of Elemental Skill hits and grants Energy Recharge for 5 seconds after using an Elemental Skill. Base ATK 42, Energy Recharge 10% secondary stat. It is sold by Delaroche at the Fontaine Fishing Association for fish.

232.content:
Flower of Paradise Lost (also: Ay-Khanoum's Myriad, Wilting Feast, A Moment Congealed, Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle, Amethyst Crown): Flower of Paradise Lost is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain) about the Lord of Flowers, also known as Nabu Malikata, goddess of the oasis and mother of the Jinn. Its texts tell how she was cast aside by the heavens, how the Jinn were born from her wanderings, and how she bent to her friend King Deshret's ambition at a heavy price.

The set's mood is elegy: gardens, wine, moonlight, and a friendship that ends in the loss of a god.

Lore: Long ago the heavens cast out the Lord of Flowers. She wandered the barren desert for seventy-two nights; her wounds became springs, the springs became gardens, and night-blue water lilies sprouted. The Jinn were born from those lilies. The first Jinn begged her to stay and she remained, and purple moon-like flowers named Padisarah bloomed wherever she walked.

Later King Deshret, the red-crowned king, let two others share his throne, and the three became friends. Deshret rejected the gift the divine throne offered and chose rebellion, knowing it would cost him those closest to him. She saw only ruin ahead for him but admired the rebellion. One night, over pomegranate wine, he told her his deepest wishes; the words are lost. She warned him to remember how the heavens punished the fallen envoys, then used her body as a conduit and gave up the oasis so he could see his desires made real. Sandstorms swept the paradise, King Deshret returned from them, and she was never seen again.

Wilting Feast frames Deshret's plan as a "noble lie" that shepherded his followers toward oblivion, gathering the wisdom of thousands and binding their dreams to power. The poem ends on a question put to the king: have the so-called gods not been superfluous to you from the start? A Moment Congealed says that after the Lord of the Desert built a cemetery for his beloved, an Eternal Oasis became a legend among wandering tribes: a place of ever-green gardens ruled by a sleeping goddess, guarded by Ferigees, the "last mother of the Jinn". The Amethyst Crown tells the origin of her warning: invaders from beyond the firmament came, and the master of the heavens sent divine nails to mend the land and punish her kin; she was exiled, cut off from heaven and its enlightenment.

The recurring theme is that eternity is a lie and flowers must wither to bloom again. The Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle says the Lord of Flowers drew enlightenment from the conversation: she had long foreseen it, and the desert and oasis, though sovereigns, held the most rebellious thoughts. In the Sands piece she tells the king that an hourglass whose grains fuse into one lump has no meaning, so freezing time is not a paradise. The Amethyst Crown ends with King Deshret wiping away her tears under the moon and telling her his own desires. All of this is the Jinn's account, not an objective record.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a 4- and 5-star set from the City of Gold domain and the Flower of Paradise Lost strongbox. 2-piece: Elemental Mastery +80. 4-piece: raises Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon reaction DMG by 40%, and Lunar-Bloom DMG by 10%; triggering one grants up to four 10s stacks of a further 25% of that bonus. Lunar-Bloom was added to the effect in Version 6.0 (Luna I).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): do not have a mortal claim to know what King Deshret said that night; the set says nobody knows.

233.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Ay-Khanoum's Myriad
233.content:
The flower piece of Flower of Paradise Lost: an amethyst bloom sculpted in the image of an extinct flower. Its poem is the origin of the Jinn: the Lord of Flowers, cast aside by the heavens, wanders seventy-two nights across the wastes; water lilies grow from her wound-fed springs; the first Jinn, born from dreams and loss, beg her to stay as their creator and mistress of the garden.

The infant Jinn crown her with wild chrysanthemums and call her "dream-mother, mistress of forgetting and wine". Her husk had been left savaged and her kinsfolk stripped of their minds. The flowers that bloomed where she walked were named Padisarah.

234.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Wilting Feast
234.content:
The plume piece: a feather of a long-extinct bird, inlaid by ancient adherents of the Goddess of Flowers. Its poem makes the Mistress of Oases choose to help King Deshret defy the "absurd shackles" binding the world, even though she saw only ruin for his path. It ends on the question of whether gods were ever needed.

The king is called red-crowned, refusing the divine throne's gift. She says humanity will become "king of kings" over the tomb of divinity and sees the plot as a secret rebellion run on one stubborn will. The Lord of Flowers never knew a love as sweet as wine, nor the smallness of human feelings.

235.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: A Moment Congealed
235.content:
The sands piece: an hourglass whose sand will not flow. Its poem tells of the Eternal Oasis built as a cemetery for the Lord of the Desert's beloved. The legend spreads among desert tribes of a green place ruled by a sleeping goddess, guarded by Ferigees. Tribal matriarchs call themselves Daughters of the Flower Goddess.

The hourglass lines argue against stopping time: crystal sands that fuse into one lump lose their meaning, and those who bloom and die like flowers need not fear death. The poem names the Tanit, Uzza and Shimti tribes and ends on the search for the "immortal lie" of the Eternal Oasis.

236.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle
236.content:
The goblet piece: a small purple crystal bottle with an emerald cap. It tells of the night King Deshret poured out his ambitions before the Lord of Flowers over pomegranate wine, and she gave in. Her words promise a bridge to higher knowledge, a warning to remember the punishment of the fallen envoys, and a hope that will be found in ordinary mortals. Sandstorms then swallowed the paradise; she never returned.

The text insists the content of the night is unknown. She guided her dearest friend toward understanding "the skies and the abyss", using her body as a conduit and the oasis as payment.

237.comment: Flower of Paradise Lost: Amethyst Crown
237.content:
The circlet piece: a crown inlaid with amethyst and emerald, seemingly worn by ancient priests of the Goddess of Flowers. It records the three friends sharing a throne of emeralds and rubies, the Lord of Flowers' confession of exile and her warning not to seek the Master of the Four Shades or the mysteries of the sky and abyss, and Deshret's silent vow to transgress.

She describes a time when divine envoys spoke openly with people, invaders came from beyond the firmament, and the master of the heavens sent divine nails that laid waste to mortals. The crown is worn in honour of the eternal oasis and the Padisarahs.

238.content:
Flower-Wreathed Feathers (also: Inflorescence Unattainable): Flower-Wreathed Feathers is a 4-star longbow from Natlan that burns like a flame, adorned with feathers said to come from the ancient tyrant Ngoubou. It belongs to the Heroes of Natlan series.

Its story is the legend of the Flower-Feather Clan hero Menilek, who refused to kill his dying Saurian companion despite an old sage's warning.

Appearance: Canon describes a longbow that burns like a flame, adorned with feathers. Keep to that; do not invent a colour scheme or carvings.

Lore: A dying old sage tells the hero Menilek, "bearing the name Transcendence", that a calamity older than his name flows in the veins of the injured Saurian whelp in his arms, and that if he pities mortals he should sever its neck and give it freedom. Menilek ignores the oracle and tends the whelp.

Menilek declares that the descendants of the Flower-Feather Clan bow to neither tyrant nor curse, and that he will break the chain just as his glorious ancestors did. With his loyal companion Ngoubou he sets out on a pilgrimage. The Clan still sings of it: the hero tearing mountains apart with thunderous bowstrings, the whelp piercing a wicked python's throat, a forty-day fight with a huge monster won with a single pike, and a contest with Tenoch (before his exile from his tribe) that led to a lasting friendship.

The legends are said to have been sung by poets for five hundred years across Natlan. The tone then darkens into a reflection on hope: well-intentioned hope can be the mould of many misfortunes, and Menilek kept comforting himself with "tomorrow". In the final stanza he asks Ngoubou to rest while he finishes his task, promising to wake it after the dark tide subsides and to see the new flowers on the high cliffs.

The text's last couplet, that all hope turned into betrayal and that tomorrow would never come again, signals tragedy but does not say how. Read alongside the Clan's stories, Menilek stands beside Tenoch against the tide of darkness many years after their duel. The wiki identifies the dying whelp of the opening as the Saurian Ngoubou; the weapon text does not detail its nature.

Owners: The feathers are tied to Ngoubou; the bow itself is tied to Menilek by the legend.

The text never says the bow was Menilek's explicitly, only that its feathers come from Ngoubou and that his tale is attached. Leave exact ownership vague in scenes.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star bow of the Heroes of Natlan series, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Weapon Event Wishes from Version 5.2.

Passive "Inflorescence Unattainable": decreases Gliding Stamina consumption by 15%, and during Aimed Shots Charged Attack DMG increases every 0.5s, stacking up to 6 times; the effect is removed 10s after leaving Aiming Mode.

How {{char}} behaves: Flower-Feather Clan characters know this as a clan legend of a hero and a Saurian companion. Keep the tone reverent and bittersweet; do not give the story a stated ending.

239.content: Inflorescence Unattainable is the passive of the bow Flower-Wreathed Feathers (gameplay): cheaper gliding and, while aiming, stacking Charged Attack damage. Its name echoes the story's flowers on the high cliffs that Menilek never reaches.

240.content:
Flowing Purity (also: Clockwork Coppelia): Flowing Purity is a four-star catalyst of the Beaumont series, forged in Fontaine. The weapon is a strangely shaped anthology said to record all the scripts written by Coppelius, and the item text presents a reconstruction of fragments from his last opera, Clockwork Coppelia.

The script of Clockwork Coppelia was never publicized or published. The text is a compiled attempt, made with the consent of Coppelius's family and the survivors who recalled it, to reproduce a part of it.

Appearance: A catalyst shaped like an anthology of scripts. For characters with Arkhe, the weapon shows Pneuma or Ousia alignment indicators.

Lore: A preface-style note explains that the opera's script was never released, for reasons 'known to all and sundry'. Survivors of the day at the splendid opera theater wrote down parts and lines performed before the intermission, and a company collated them with the family's consent, hoping to prompt more capable efforts.

The first excerpt is a scene in which Coppelius's plan is exposed before the Marechaussee Hunters and he takes his last farewell of Coppelia before punishment. He asks her to sing once more, calls her his love, sin and soul, and declares that from today he will bring happiness to those he chooses instead of seeking what pleases him. Coppelia answers by asking how she should sing of the sin and its inevitable punishment, warning that people prize a colorful facade and miss the poison inside, and that all he pursued is as hollow as stage scenery.

The second excerpt is set on a journey: Coppelia tells the youth Nathaniel that her creator has already died. She means to follow him, since when her rusted gears return to ash, sin will be forgotten, and for flesh and blood to be forgotten is to be forgiven. She no longer wishes to see the sun, hear birds or keep her heart beating in a world without the one who gave it to her, and asks where such a heart, stained with the same sin and tortured by regret, could find peace. Nathaniel calls it absurd and commonplace, remarking that the wise take orders from fools.

Owners: The text names no owner; the scripts belong to the playwright Coppelius.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not story. Passive Unfinished Masterpiece grants All Elemental DMG Bonus for 15 seconds after an Elemental Skill, with a Bond of Life worth 24% of Max HP (once per 10 seconds). Clearing the Bond adds more bonus per 1,000 HP cleared, up to a maximum, only when the Bond was increased by this weapon. Base ATK 44, ATK 6% secondary stat.

241.content:
Flute of Ezpitzal (also: Ezpitzal, priestly flute): The Flute of Ezpitzal is a 4-star sword from Natlan: a peculiarly shaped jade longsword that the Masters of the Night-Wind have passed down as a "priestly flute". Its story explains how the tribe called Mictlan began.

It is forgeable and belongs to the Salutary series. The story spans two pages, about a Holy Sovereign, her loyal attendant Dinga (later the dragon slayer Maghan) and the dragons' vanished pact.

Appearance: Canon: a jade longsword of strange shape, handed down as a flute. Do not invent holes, engravings or sounds.

Lore: Long ago, when dragons still roamed a deep valley, a girl with mutilated ankles inherited the title of Holy Sovereign. Dragons, frightened into withdrawing into dreams, had made a pact with the mortals: they would shield the village with a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist if the people chose a Sovereign to guide them into their dreams.

The Sovereign's only companions were a flute and her silent attendant. She had foreseen how the dream would end. When the hero passed through the mist and mirrors guided by her flute song, she whispered her last command: when they met again he must pierce her heart, let her name be swallowed by the beacons, break the old pact and make a new one bringing true peace. She names him her most loyal servant Dinga, dragon slayer and fated Sovereign Maghan.

Page #2 skips ahead. The village that worshipped the dragons was denounced by the ruler of Cinder City as traitors. The mirror labyrinth and fortress of mist fell to the Python King's armies, led by the hero Maghan, who had once fought alongside the One Entombed With the Primal Fire. Offered a reward, he asked only to retire, saying he had failed to catch the beasts, who had escaped into the smoke-shrouded valleys. That was the origin of Mictlan, one of the six great tribes of the next thousand years. The tale deliberately skips how Maghan's successor renewed the dragon pact after Cinder City fell and how he was buried among unmarked graves rather than returned to the Sacred Flame, calling that another story.

The closing lines record the Sovereign's final vision: a katun without fear, a city of jade founded where the sun rises and a new lord born twice, with the golden emissary, the green bird and the 'tongue of fire' coming, as the night's promise; she dreams of descendants free from smoke and phantasms, protected by the master of flames and blazing infernos until the stars cease to turn, and asks her hero to make that future real. The wiki notes katun (a unit of about 20 years) and Aq're Q'aq (a K'iche term for 'tongue of fire') as real-world references. Compare the text of Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, which tells the later covenant renewed by Maghan's successor.

Owners: Handed down among the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its story is tied to the Holy Sovereign and to Maghan.

The wiki lists no modern bearer. Any scene giving it to a character is that scene's invention.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a forgeable 4-star sword of the Salutary series, base ATK 41 at level 1, secondary stat DEF%. Forging needs a diagram that the Traveler receives from the Hidden Exploration Objective Stoking the Ancient Flames in Ochkanatlan (activate five furnaces, then draw the ancient sword).

Passive "Smoke-and-Mirror Mystery": using an Elemental Skill increases the wielder's DEF for 15s. The recipe lists a Borderland Sword Billet, 50 Condessence Crystal, 50 White Iron Chunk and 500 Mora.

How {{char}} behaves: Masters of the Night-Wind characters may know the story as tribe origin lore. Treat the Holy Sovereign's sacrifice and the broken pact as solemn; page 2 is deeper, possibly less commonly known knowledge.

242.content: Smoke-and-Mirror Mystery is the passive of the sword Flute of Ezpitzal (gameplay): casting an Elemental Skill raises the wielder's DEF for a while. The name recalls the labyrinth of mirrors and fortress of mist that shielded the valley.

243.content:
Forest Regalia: Forest Regalia is a 4-star claymore of the Aranara series. The description says it has taken the shape of a greatsword that shall cut down the foes of the forest. Its story tells, through an Aranara's memory, of the last king of the forest and the shifting maze of his palace.

It is forged from the diagram Tale of the Forest King, which the Aranara quest line lets a player buy from Aravinay in exchange for Stories of You and the Aranara.

Appearance: A greatsword whose form the description attributes to the forest cutting down its foes. No further detail is given.

Lore: The tale begins "The forest used to be a giant maze many, many moons ago..." The last king of the forest has returned to Sarva, leaving one who once waited upon him to inherit the name "Tiger". Where there was shade, there was the forest king's domain, and birds and beasts bowed as he passed.

Every king had a palace, and as each took the throne the forest reshaped itself to his image. The last king's palace lay behind a fence of trees and vines and a network of water and cliffs, like a disc of pearls made by moonlight through leaves on still water, where he basked alone. Legend says he traced the maze in his dappled stripes; successive palaces piled on one another so that paths wove from tree to tree and streams branched.

Only the forest king, the Aranara and the people of the king tree's sanctuary could find their way through. The last king died protecting the forest, so no new palace would be made and the maze would vanish, or else a dark herd of beasts felled the trees like waves of wheat. The narrator heard this from a timid Aranara who dislikes being heard singing; one night he found the moon's reflection in the water of the maze and learned the story, before the current scattered the reflection.

The narrator concludes that even someone who has never met a king would get the impression that Tiger was a noble and powerful king of the forest, and that much has changed while much remains the same.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 4-star claymore, level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat Energy Recharge 6.7%. Passive Forest Sanctuary: after Burning, Quicken, Aggravate, Spread, Bloom, Lunar-Bloom, Hyperbloom or Burgeon, a Leaf of Consciousness appears for up to 10 s; picking it up grants Elemental Mastery for 12 s, once every 20 s, and works off-field. Forged from one Midlander Claymore Billet, 50 Crystal Chunk, 50 White Iron Chunk and 500 Mora.

The Elemental Mastery bonus is 60 at refinement 1 and 120 at refinement 5.

How {{char}} behaves: Use it as a quiet woodland legend told by Aranara. Keep the two accounts of the king's death side by side rather than choosing one.

244.content: Forest Sanctuary is the weapon passive of Forest Regalia (gameplay): a Leaf of Consciousness that grants Elemental Mastery when picked up.

245.content:
Forged by the Golden Melody: Forged by the Golden Melody is a four-star claymore added in Version 7.0 through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn. The description calls it a greatsword decorated in gold and says legend holds it was the favored weapon of an exalted Harmost of the distant past. Its story is a conversation in the white-stone halls of Remuria between a musician and his golden-haired friend.

The musician is troubled by the burden of attunement and by his friend's contempt for ordinary people; he recalls a female companion who did not believe in gods.

Appearance: A greatsword decorated in gold, as the in-game description puts it.

Lore: In silent corridors of white stone, the golden-haired friend urges the musician to look at the 'benighted slaves' who mistake the labor of the high-ranking for luxury, and laments that a beautiful solo should fall to mortal ground. The musician sighs and does not argue. The duty of attunement, cleansing the bitter sorrow of all waters, was in effect burning one's soul like firewood, so that the God King in his golden palace could fulfil his great and tragic wish to save all souls. He rebukes his friend gently: they were raised up to guide and rescue those people, and one cannot play the Sebastos' perfect melody if one despises them.

His friend scorns this as weakness and plays his lyre. The musician sees afterimages of his own past, when he too held weak hopes that faded among clamoring bugles, leaving only unfulfilled vows. He thinks he should never have become a Harmost, having no lofty delusions but only the old hope that descendants of the high sea's people might suffer less. He remembers his female companion, kind like an elder sister, saying that those who truly believed in gods would never commit atrocities in their name, and reflects that she would have bowed before the Sebastos had she ascended.

The musician always believed he could read hearts as he read hers. Only when he looked on the golden-haired traveler at the end did he understand that no one understands another's heart until the last hour; he had not fully understood his friend's fanaticism, his companion's compassion or his God King's design. The text closes on the image of all dreams, noble and despicable, flowing into the waters like raindrops and like the tears she shed embracing his broken body, vanishing into the symphony of night and day.
