A hero called Erinnyes in these tales has nothing to do with the real woman who shared the name, and the ballads are "dreams of the present".
Cross-check with wider canon (not in these pieces): the Remurian empire was led by Remus with four human Harmosts (Boethius and Cassiodor among them), and Cassiodor shared a tribe with Erinnyes, who left for Egeria's side. This is why the identification of the songstress with Erinnyes and the musician with Cassiodor is common but remains interpretation. The Lochknights became a Fontainian legend, and the "Pure Grail" tale was heard in La Chanson d'Erinnyes.

The set deliberately includes the tension between what happened and how it is remembered: Poetry of Days Past warns that later heroic verse is not the true past, and Promised Dream shows the Grail belief to be hearsay from an ancient Oceanid's words. The vows of Forgotten Oath are presented as constants of every retelling, but the details of the pledge differ between versions.

Owners: No named owner; narrative item text only.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the 2-piece bonus is Healing Bonus +15%. The 4-piece effect creates a Yearning effect for 6s when the wearer heals a party member, recording total healing including overflow (up to 15,000), then converts it to Waves of Days Past, adding 8% of the recorded total to the active character's DMG for the next 5 hits or 10s. Standby wearers still trigger it. Obtained from the Waterfall Wen domain in Fontaine and the artifact strongbox. Added in Version 4.3.

Waterfall Wen is a Domain of Blessing on the east slopes of Mont Automnequi in Fontaine's Morte Region: a sunken ruin once used by a secret order, now ruled by beasts without language.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): lean into the set's elegy: memorial verse, bells, silver and gold. Remind characters that stories of Lochknights are partly legend, as the circlet itself says.

608.comment: Song of Days Past: Lochknight (set lore)
608.content: In Forgotten Oath of Days Past, the first Lochknight is the unnamed oracle-songstress who united northern tribes against Remuria and swore to Egeria, with two vows: never draw the sword on those who pledge faith in Egeria, and never tolerate evil. Poetry of Days Past shows how later poems retold her, and the Lochknights have their own entry.

609.comment: Song of Days Past: Pure Grail
609.content: In this set the Pure Grail is a legendary vessel of primordial water said to heal, restore youth, revive the dead and grant any wish. No one in the pieces has seen it, the belief came from an Oceanid's words, and it is called a heterodoxy. Poetry of Days Past retells the quest as myth.

key: Dawn and Dusk by the Lake
610.content:
Splendor of Tranquil Waters (also: Hauteclaire, Dawn and Dusk by the Lake): Splendor of Tranquil Waters is a 5-star sword: a scepter around which pure water swirls, once a symbol of the highest authority over the seas. Its story belongs to Erinnyes, a figure of the age of Remuria.

The description exists in two versions that disagree about what Erinnyes was and what she achieved, which makes the sword a good example of how Fontaine's legends are told in more than one way.

Appearance: Canon gives only: a scepter wrapped in swirling pure water, water-blue in colour, with a pommel tip that glows with Pneuma or Ousia light when held by a character who has an Arkhe alignment. Add no further detail.

Lore: A scepter that once symbolised supreme authority over the seas. It belonged to Erinnyes, who in the time of the great symphony united the people of the high waters against the gods.

The legend says her home was destroyed early by the God King, Remus, whose army from the Golden City enslaved or killed her family. Only two escaped. One met the proud Harmost during the war and rose to inherit his authority (the wiki links this person to Cassiodor and the Harmost to Boethius). The other was taken in by the Prince (page 1) or chieftain (page 2) of Aremorica to guard the waters the God King had not yet seized. The text frames them as two survivors of one home drifting apart, one toward good and one toward evil.

Page 1 tells it as a knightly quest. Sworn in Egeria's name to find the Pure Grail and free her, Erinnyes and her fellow knights (linked to the Lochknights) suffer terrible trials; their pure hearts and the Grail, won through sacrifice, restore the Mistress of Many Waters. Burdened by the sins of her deeds, Erinnyes then asks Egeria to judge and expel her. The goddess, believing a fair verdict is the greatest mercy to a selfless soul, grants it. The sword sinks into the lake with Egeria's blessing, and Erinnyes departs with her head high, never seen again.

Page 2 tells it as a revenge story. The sword-singer swears to retrieve the Grail and break her mother goddess's shackles, but never finds it. The heavens themselves choose the Mistress of Many Waters, ordering her back from her prison to succeed the golden king and rule the sea-ruins. Erinnyes begs that goddess for wisdom on how the descendants of the seas can avoid disaster, saying she killed the unrighteous and toppled cities for her. The goddess answers with what she once told the King of Fortuna, and the plea ends in despair: the sword, stained with blood, falls away with Erinnyes's last thread of reason, and she is never seen again.

Page 2 closes on a note about memory: the chieftain who dreamed of honour and glory never saw the land of her dreams and never found absolution, like a goddess who shared similar hopes. Many years later the musician called the Golden Hunter (linked to Cassiodor) recalls the name and thinks neither of blood nor tears, only of a distant flute and a twisting melody under a watery moon. Page 1 by contrast ends on the departing knight and the sunk sword, with no mention of the flute.

The wiki credits the book La Chanson d'Erinnyes with the information that the sword was called Hauteclaire in Remurian times. Treat that as an alias attributed to the book, not as something the weapon text itself says.

Owners: Erinnyes, per the description. No present-day wielder is named.

Furina is the character this sword is usually paired with, but only as a gameplay and release-timing convention (see uncertainties). Do not state in narration that she inherited or found it unless the user's scenario does.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star sword, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 4.2. Passive "Dawn and Dusk by the Lake": when the wielder's current HP increases or decreases, their Elemental Skill DMG rises for a few seconds (stacking up to 3 times); when other party members' HP changes, the wielder's Max HP rises (stacking up to 2 times). Both can trigger off-field. Values scale with refinement.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: speak of the sword as a scepter tied to old legends of Egeria and the people of the seas, and keep the two accounts of Erinnyes both available. A character can know one version, a stage play or a song, without the other. Do not resolve which is true.

611.comment: Splendor of Tranquil Waters: Erinnyes and Hauteclaire
611.content: The scepter Splendor of Tranquil Waters is tied to the legend of Erinnyes: a figure of Remurian times who united rebellious people of the high waters, with two conflicting tellings of her quest for the Pure Grail and her plea to Egeria. The wiki says it was once called Hauteclaire, citing the book La Chanson d'Erinnyes.

612.content:
Staff of Homa (also: Homa Staff, Hùmó zhī Zhàng): The Staff of Homa is a five-star polearm of Liyue: a "devilishly red" ritual staff from the Archon War era, when fire rites were used to cleanse the miasmas of dead gods. Item text says a merciful doctor was given it by a whispering flame and used it to burn away impurity and release the dead from their ill karma. Today it is carried by Hu Tao, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's director, who inherited it through the Hu family.

Its name echoes homa, a fire-offering ritual. The wiki also notes the winged top of the staff, possibly a nod to the Homa bird of Persian myth. Nothing in the item text states the staff is a weapon first: Hu Tao's friend Xiangling does not know much about it beyond what Hu Tao has told her.

Appearance: Item text calls it a "devilishly red" staff and, in the doctor's vision, "scarlet firewood". The wiki records a winged motif at the top, which it says matches the wings of Ronova; the item text itself describes no wings.

Lore: The item story: rites that cleanse by fire let impurity rise with the flames to the heavens. Fresh cinders were lit in rainy seasons and wolf smoke rose as prayers for blessings and the defeat of evil. These rites were common in the ancient period of strife, since the dreams and delusions of the silent corpses of gods bred evil miasmas that snatched away citizens.

A merciful doctor then heard a whisper from within a flame as red as the sunset, from the crackling of withered grass: "Only an unbound flame can purify the filth of this world", and "Lift up this scarlet firewood. With it, you shall repel every demon." The doctor took up the red staff and burned all that was impure. The dead, who could not bear their sorrow and had been shrouded in ill karma and calamity, were reduced in the flame to ashen butterflies and found relief. Legend says the doctor, who lit countless flames, was likewise reduced to smoke shaped like a lovely butterfly. The rites were forgotten with the coming of peace, but those with fire in their hearts can still hear the whispered words when facing a great darkness.

The wiki reads the rites as the origin of the Wangsheng arts and the staff as a ceremonial tool, not an ordinary weapon, and describes the Wangsheng spear techniques as using polearms and purifying flames meant to destroy demons. It also suggests the staff was used to purify bodies during the plague after the Yaksha's accumulated karma killed many in Liyue (marked "likely"). Because the whisper and the staff's wing design match Ronova, the wiki's Ronova page suggests she was the voice; the Ronova connection is still only the wiki's inference. Treat all of these as readings of a poetic text.

Owners: Current owner: Hu Tao, director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, per the wiki's reading of the Lantern Rite event Springtime Charms (5.3, limited-time) as showing it passed down through the Hu family. The doctor of the legend is unnamed; the wiki treats the first wielder as heavily implied to be a Hu family ancestor.

Zhongli temporarily holds the staff in some one-time story domains and trial runs, before returning to the Vortex Vanquisher; that is a gameplay stand-in, not a change of owner.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star polearm from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat CRIT DMG 14.4%. Passive "Reckless Cinnabar": HP rises 20-40% and the wielder gains ATK equal to 0.8-1.6% of Max HP, plus a further 1-1.8% of Max HP while HP is under 50% (refinements 1 to 5).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): the staff is a funeral-rite object first, so its owners treat it with ritual seriousness even when playful. Sparks, drifting ember and butterfly motifs fit; avoid presenting it as a casual spear that any Liyue guard might carry.

613.comment: Staff of Homa: Hu Tao and the staff
613.content: The Lantern Rite event Springtime Charms (5.3) is cited by the wiki for showing Hu Tao as the staff's current owner, passed down through the Hu family. Xiangling, her best friend, does not know much about the staff beyond what Hu Tao has told her.

614.comment: Staff of Homa: Wangsheng rites and the doctor
614.content: In the Staff of Homa legend, fire rites in the rainy season with wolf smoke served as prayers against the miasmas of dead gods. The doctor who received the staff is unnamed. Treat any link from the doctor to the Hu family or to a particular adeptus as the wiki's inference, not a stated fact.

615.content:
Staff of the Scarlet Sands: The Staff of the Scarlet Sands is a 5-star polearm of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it one of a paired set of obsidian scepters that grant the right to lead the people of the desert, though no retainer now lives who can verify the proper appearance of these regalia. Its story is a monologue by King Deshret about how the world should be ordered, ending in his longing for a perfect world.

The staff is the polearm partner of the Key of Khaj-Nisut. Together the wiki treats them as keys to the Orchard of Pairidaeza, the eternal oasis made as Nabu Malikata's resting place.

Appearance: An obsidian scepter or staff. Canon text gives no more detail. The in-game description stresses that no one is left alive who can confirm what the genuine regalia looked like, so depictions are uncertain.

Lore: The narrator, speaking as a creator, lists how the world was made: the sun and three moons (as a woman once described them to him), weight so that sand sank into earth, and seven sage monks to rule the paths of earth, water and stars. After the original world's barriers fell and dark poison seeped in, spikes pierced the earth to heal it.

He then lists what must be removed for his ideal: the cycle of seven, the barrier between life and death, the sun, moons and weight, the original rules and verdicts, and all creatures, so that none steal wisdom. He pictures the Sand King sleeping alone, drawing up new theorems, and "our paradise" regained; that oasis was never a paradise for the many.

The text ends with a request: the narrator does not want the poison taken in by mistake to remain in the world, and hopes "she" (the wiki identifies the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata) might, for old friendship, help; if not for his sake then for their mutual friend. Per the wiki, the text is Deshret speaking about his friend Nabu Malikata, an exiled Seelie, and the punishment placed on the Seelie after the war. The wiki ties the "spikes" to the Celestial Nails and the war to the one in which the Dragon King Nibelung brought the Abyss to Teyvat; this is its cross-reference of other sources.

Two things should be kept apart. The statements in the text are the narrator's own plan and wishes: he considers his rules "more elegant and precise" than the existing ones. The wiki additionally reads the later quest events (the spread of the forbidden knowledge as plagues in Deshret's civilisation and Rukkhadevata's intervention, which cost her power) as the answer to the request. Treat that last part as a reading of other quests, not as something the staff's text confirms.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. Cyno appears with the ascended staff in his official art and character demo, and Candace with the unascended one in her wish art and TCG card (wiki trivia).

Per the wiki, Cyno names the staff as his weapon in the After Repose quest. As canon is not explicit on whether the objects shown are the original regalia, do not claim any character holds the original scepter.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): 5-star polearm released in Version 3.1 (2022-09-28), level 1 base ATK 44, secondary stat CRIT Rate. Passive Heat Haze at Horizon's End gives bonus ATK equal to a percentage of the wielder's Elemental Mastery; when an Elemental Skill hits opponents, the Dream of the Scarlet Sands effect adds more for 10 s, up to 3 stacks. Multiple targets hit give multiple stacks, and the effect is not gained off-field.

At refinement 1 the base conversion is 52% of Elemental Mastery and each stack adds 28%; refinement 5 gives 104% and 56%. Ascension uses Chaos Storage, Chaos Module and Chaos Bolt with Fungal Spores, Luminescent Pollen and Crystalline Cyst Dust.

How {{char}} behaves: The staff suits discussions of Deshret's age: scholars and priests may mention scepters that confer the right to lead the desert's people. Keep the uncertainty the description itself states: nobody can say what the regalia truly looked like.

616.comment: Staff of the Scarlet Sands: Heat Haze at Horizon's End
616.content: Heat Haze at Horizon's End is the weapon passive of the Staff of the Scarlet Sands (gameplay). It turns Elemental Mastery into attack and adds a stacking effect after Elemental Skill hits, named for a dream of the scarlet sands.

617.content:
Starcaller's Watch (also: Offering Unto Wind and Sun, Mirror of Night): Starcaller's Watch is a 5-star catalyst: a statue carved in the shape of an eagle, a sacred relic of the Masters of the Night-Wind passed down from generation to generation.

Its story is about the girl chosen to guide the people into night's slumber, and about the man who believed he could manipulate her.

Appearance: A statue carved in the shape of an eagle; the story calls it a statuette and associates eagle feathers with the star-caller's crown. Add no other details.

Lore: In an ancient, exalted contract the messenger of night chose a child with a star-bright soul, set a crown of eagle feathers on her brow, and charged her to guide a formless ancient people into night's slumber.

The text pictures her as a young woman, once kneeling before dragons, who later turned and led an outlander through a wall of fumes with flute and song.

A self-proclaimed sage (the wiki identifies him with Waxaklahun Ubah Kan) schemed in the dragons' dreams. A covenant between the valley people and the noble scions cut off the war-chiefs' bloodlust and left only the silence of death on the shrouded paths, so that even the bravest warrior of the Tezcatepetonco valley served the star-caller. The sage disliked the decay of the fallen and used small tricks to incite her to rebel against the dragons, believing human hearts easy to steer: add fuel to suffering, speak of hope, and she hung on his words.

As he had predicted, she led an outlander the sage had never seen through the fumes, and sent her silent servant Dinga from the deep valley. He expected the flames of slaughter to be drawn to this isolated land.

Many years later, when the hero Maghan plunged the Python King's golden dagger into his former master's heart, the sage realized that the seeds of betrayal had long been planted: not aimed at the sleeping dragons as he had imagined, but carried alongside the song of the newborn Wayob from the deepest halls of the Night Realm. This secured the foundations of the tribe called "Mictlan" for a thousand years. The seven-layered curtains in the cell sealed the ancient, lightless land of disorder, and ants stole the secret rites the sage could never obtain.

The closing words are the girl's own, in the wiki's reading: do not put all hope in the night or the benevolence of saints, and above all do not trust the one who calls himself a sage; humans can rely only on themselves. Even if all goes as she intends she will only stabilize the boundary for a hundred years, so Dinga must tell the people of the tribes of their heroes, stretch their memories out on woven scrolls and anchor this home that will be named Natlan. She gives him the statuette and promises to watch over him, bound to his shoulder like a silken string, until their souls are entwined in profound peace.

Owners: The Masters of the Night-Wind keep it as a sacred relic. The wiki names its first wielder as the Holy Sovereign who was Maghan's master.

Maghan (earlier named Dinga) is given the statuette in the story's last lines. No source shown establishes who holds it now, and Citlali is not stated to carry it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat Elemental Mastery; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.3. The passive only triggers while the wielder is on-field.

Passive "Offering Unto Wind and Sun": Elemental Mastery is increased (100 at refinement 1 up to 200 at refinement 5). Within 15s after the wielder creates a shield, "Mirror of Night" makes the active character deal 28% to 56% more DMG to nearby opponents, once every 14s. Ascension uses Sacred Lord Delirious materials, Will-series boss materials and whistle common materials.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: shamans of the Masters of the Night-Wind may regard the watch as a keepsake of the first Holy Sovereign. They should speak of the girl and Maghan with respect, and leave the sage's role as the text frames it (a schemer outplayed).

618.comment: Starcaller's Watch: Offering Unto Wind and Sun
618.content: Offering Unto Wind and Sun is the passive of the catalyst Starcaller's Watch (gameplay): an Elemental Mastery boost, plus the Mirror of Night damage bonus for the active character after the wielder creates a shield.

619.content: Per the wiki, Maghan's master was the last Holy Sovereign of the tribe in the Tezcatepetonco Range that became Mictlan. Her servant Dinga later became Maghan; he killed her on Och-Kan's orders, and after her death she became the tribe's Wayob. The Starcaller's Watch text is told in her voice and is the source for her being its first wielder.

620.content:
Starsilver (also: Starsilver ore, Starsilver Ore): Starsilver is a rare, precious ore found only on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. Its item text says it is formed by the mountain's unique geography and its ley lines. It is silvery, is worked in forges, and is also prized by artists as a pigment source.

Smiths use it to forge Fine Enhancement Ore and several weapons, notably the Dragonspine series. In the mountain's old lore a Starsilver greatsword was handed by the princess of Sal Vindagnyr to the outlander Imunlaukr.

Despite the name, canon never says Starsilver fell from the sky or came from stars. It is a native ore of a mountain that was long a scene of ancient catastrophe, and it turns up in several of that mountain's stories.

Appearance: A silver-coloured ore. Albedo notes that even impure Starsilver contains fine silver-coloured particles, but that lower grades lack luster, while good specimens have great luster and a lovely colour. Escoffier reports that it tastes like snow and ice mixed with limewash paint.

Lore: Its item text calls it a rare and precious ore formed by Dragonspine's unique geographical conditions and ley lines. In the Snow-Tombed Starsilver text, the greatsword is forged from Starsilver and able to cleave ice and snow. The weapon lore has the princess of Sal Vindagnyr give it to Imunlaukr as he left to search for a way to end the frost; he later returned it, and it came to rest between the frescoes of the mural room.

The Disaster and Remorse text, released in Version 6.6, has the same warrior hurl an astral-silver lance, described as made of Whitestone and Starsilver, in defence of a maiden. Those weapon entries tell the human stories; this entry only records that Starsilver is the metal in them. The wiki groups the forged Dragonspine weapons as the Dragonspine (or Starsilver) series, whose shared lore concerns what was entombed in the mountain's cold: a people, a tree and a dragon.

In the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (limited-time, Act I: The Snowy Past), Albedo is found on Dragonspine gathering Starsilver for silver paint, having run out of his previous batch. The quest has the Traveler collect one Inferior Starsilver (dull and low in luster, unlikely to sell high) and one Quality Starsilver (great luster, lovely colour) near the cavern entrance. Earlier, in The First Experiment: Elements (Version 1.2), Albedo identifies a Starsilver Catalyst, ore that looks like ordinary Starsilver but that he can use as an alchemical catalyst.

Owners: No notable owner. Albedo uses it for paint, smiths for forging, and in old Dragonspine legend its metal was carried as a greatsword by Imunlaukr and as a lance in the Disaster and Remorse tale.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: a forging material added in Version 1.2, mined only on Dragonspine from destructible ore nodes that drop 1-3 each and respawn after 48 hours. Blunt attacks and Geo abilities break the nodes fastest, and Anemo cannot move the drops.

Three Starsilver forge one Fine Enhancement Ore (weapon experience). The 4-star Dragonspine series, with the Frost Burial passive, requires 30 Northlander Billets and 30 Starsilver among its materials. Starsilver Catalyst, Inferior Starsilver and Quality Starsilver are quest items and cannot be used like the ore.

621.content: During the Shadows Amidst Snowstorms event, Albedo says Starsilver makes high-quality silver paint and that he has run out of his last batch. Only luminous, low-impurity ore is suitable: dull specimens give a paint seen as a fake or defective product. He collects the ore himself on Dragonspine, which he also finds a quiet place to gather his thoughts.

622.content:
String of Pearls (also: String of Pearls play, Lian Xin Zhu): String of Pearls is a five-act Liyue opera script by Yun Jin, split into five volumes. It follows Zixin, a young fisherwoman, and Fan Jie, a dock worker who returns her lost string of pearls. A misunderstanding, a false reward notice, a local bully named Wu Wang and a rescue in a dark stronghold bring them together.

The script is written as stage directions, role lists and sung lines in the "Dongtang" and "Ganging" styles. It uses stock roles of opera: a male lead, a female lead, a comic role and a villain. A comic character, Grandma Zhang, speaks to the audience and mentions Yun Jin's plays directly.

Appearance: Printed script pages with an act title, a cast list and numbered scenes. Delivery notes in brackets (aside, aloud, and musical directions like lento or appassionato) mix with stage movements.

Lore: Act I, Of Fish and Water: Zixin, sixteen by her own line, sells fish to support her ageing parents. She loses her string of pearls and Fan Jie, who found it, checks her wrist for wear marks. She takes this as an insult and scolds him before learning he meant well. He leaves before telling his full name, and she regrets it.

- Humour and structure: the comic roles break the fourth wall, remark on Yun Jin's plays and theatre convention, and parody the reward trope. Wu Wang is a cartoonish bully who thinks nothing of unpaid meals and kidnapping.
- Themes are modest honesty and mistaken first impressions; the pearls link the pair in Acts I, III and V.

- Scene use: quote only a line or two. It suits an audience at a Liyue theatre, a bookhouse conversation or a scene where Yun Jin or an opera fan discusses the plot.

Owners: No owner; the volumes are spread through Liyue Harbor. Yun Jin is the credited author.

Gameplay: Game note: a book collection with no stats. Vol. 1 is at Third-Round Knockout on the table Jiangzhou sits at during the night; Vols. 2 and 3 are sold by Jifang at Wanwen Bookhouse; Vol. 4 is on the bookhouse roof; Vol. 5 is next to Geri.

623.comment: String of Pearls: Zixin and Fan Jie
623.content: Zixin and Fan Jie are the leads of the opera String of Pearls. Zixin is a fisherwoman who sells fish in Liyue Harbor. Fan Jie is a dock worker chosen by fellow workers as leader. He returns her pearls, and after misunderstandings and a rescue from Wu Wang they plan to marry. They are stage characters from Yun Jin's script.

624.comment: String of Pearls: String of Pearls Act Summaries
624.content:
- Act II, The Search for the Gentleman: on Grandma Zhang's advice Zixin posts a Mora reward notice to find him. Three tricksters, Zhang San, Li Si and Wang Er'ma, try to claim it with false goods. Grandma Zhang drives them off with a trap, Fan Jie is brought in by mistake, and the two realise the misunderstanding and apologise to one another.
- Act III, The Pearls, Lost Again: the two meet daily. The local bully Wu Wang, with companions Wu Yi and Wu Er, seizes Zixin. Grandma Zhang gives Fan Jie the pearls, and he rides to rescue her.
- Act IV, Trial by Candlelight: Fan Jie scouts Wu Wang's stronghold. Zixin hits the drunk Wu Wang with a candlestick and flees in the dark without relighting it.
- Act V, Twin Pearls Returned: in the dark, Fan Jie and Zixin find each other, Wu Wang mistakes Fan Jie for someone else and is stabbed, and the couple leave together with a promise.

625.content:
Sturdy Bone (also: Trapper's Pride, Wanjiru's bone sword): Sturdy Bone is a 4-star longsword from Natlan, made of bone that has only grown harder with use. Legend says it was the hero Wanjiru's reliable weapon.

Its story shows Wanjiru, famous for strength, slipping into the great dragon's tomb for a weapon and coming back with a bone in her palm.

Appearance: A longsword made of bleached bone, the spit of a giant beast's tail in the story. Do not invent engravings or a handle design beyond a hilt.

Lore: The great dragon that once ruled the land of flame had a tomb of bleached bone ridges like giant claws, patrolled by secret machines. Hearing of it around the tribe's fire, Wanjiru leaps for joy: nothing in the world was more fearsome, and surely she could find there the weapon she wanted most.

The text lists her feats: shattering century-old ironwood with a swing, crushing raw ore to powder, bending boulders and toughest metal in her fingers. She jumps into the volcano from Tollan's peak, avoids the serpent-like guardian constructs and enters the ruins, following scars left by the heroes who once fought the dragon. She wishes she had been born in those days. The boneyard seems only a place of lonely corpses until a huge winged golden shadow throws itself at her.

She fights it with a laugh in a bloody, eye-for-an-eye brawl and ends it by tearing off its shattered wing with her bare hands. The shadow vanishes with a wail as if it had never been real. She finds her hand still outstretched, her arm aching and a heavy dragon bone in her palm shaped like the tail of the beast she had grappled.

When she tells her story-loving friends, the High Priest of the Night-Wind scrunches his nose and says Tollan is forbidden ground and she was too young then; another friend holding a ceremonial blade says they have never even seen her draw the weapon. She replies that she just usually doesn't need to. On the eve of battle by the campfire, seeing the great black beast's silhouette on the shore, she grips the hilt of the bleached bone blade and waits for the battlefield where she will draw it once more. The wiki links the black beast to the Abyss; the text itself says only that she keeps the blade in reserve for that battle.

Owners: Wanjiru, by the text's legend. No later wielder is named.

Her friends doubt the dragon-tomb tale, so ownership rests on her word and on the weapon description rather than on witnessed events.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword of the Heroes of Natlan series, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat ATK%. Weapon Event Wishes from Version 5.1.

Passive "Trapper's Pride": decreases Sprint or Alternate Sprint Stamina consumption by 15%; after sprinting, Normal Attack DMG is increased by a percentage of ATK (16% at refinement 1 up to 32% at refinement 5) until 18 triggers or 7s.

How {{char}} behaves: Natlanese storytellers may tell it as a boast: Wanjiru proved herself, though her friends teased her about the story.

626.content: Trapper's Pride is the passive of the sword Sturdy Bone (gameplay): sprinting costs less Stamina and the next Normal Attacks hit harder for a short time.

627.content:
Summit Shaper (also: Zhuófēng zhī Rèn, Blade of Mountain Cut): Summit Shaper is a five-star sword of Liyue and one of the Liyue series weapons tied to Rex Lapis in the Archon War. Item text says that in an age of turmoil, when people cried out for lost loved ones, the ruler of Geo carved a long blade from a slab of golden Cor Lapis, cut a corner off a mountain with one stroke, and on it swore a solemn oath: to gather the scattered and punish those who broke contracts.

The text says the oath still works in Liyue: to break a contract is to make an enemy of the land, and the mountain Rex Lapis cut will sooner or later fall on contract-breakers. A legend adds that the sword's true owner will one day return among mortals.

Appearance: Item text describes a long blade carved from a pure slab of golden Cor Lapis and says that when its owner returns it "will once again gleam gold". It gives no hilt or length details.

Lore: The story begins with ordinary people asking where their lovers and children had gone, when the departed would return and how long the horrors would last. Even hearts hewn from bedrock cracked, and the eyes of those who kept faithful silence began to smolder.

In answer the ruler of Geo (Morax) put forth his might, carved the blade, sliced a corner from a mountain and swore on it: scattered people would be gathered, contract-breakers punished, and those who lost loved ones, possessions or justice would receive recompense. The text admits this is but one of many tales about ancient Liyue, yet claims the oath is at work in the land: breaking a contract makes an enemy of the country where gods once ruled.

The closing legend says the weapon's true owner will return to walk among mortals; the sword will gleam gold again and its light will cut through the world's greatest injustices, as it did at the oath. The wiki's Liyue Series page uses the story as an example of Morax's weapons in the Archon War and does not claim the return has happened.

Owners: The text credits the sword to the ruler of Geo, Morax or Rex Lapis. It records no later holder, and canon does not show Zhongli carrying it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star sword from weapon event wishes. Base ATK 46, secondary stat ATK 10.8%. Passive "Golden Majesty", shared by the Liyue series: Shield Strength +20-40% and scoring hits raises ATK 4-8% for 8 seconds, up to 5 stacks, doubled while under a shield (refinements 1 to 5).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): Liyue's contract culture makes this a natural touchstone for talk of oaths, honesty and the cost of breaking a deal. Present it as a legend told in Liyue, not as an object a character can produce.

628.content: The Liyue series is an unofficial grouping of five-star weapons tied to Morax in the Archon War, sharing the passive "Golden Majesty" and the stats of base ATK 46 and ATK 10.8% (before levelling). The wiki lists Summit Shaper and Vortex Vanquisher among them and describes the series as weapons closely associated with Morax in the Archon War.

629.content:
Sunny Morning Sleep-In (also: Bathhouses, Hawks, and Narukami): Sunny Morning Sleep-In is a five-star catalyst, a bell lantern forged from purple jade. The game description says that placed beside a pillow it brings sweet dreams. Its item story is a sad, quiet one about a shrine maiden who had the three auspicious "first dreams" of the new year before the Cataclysm, and whose dreams of bathhouses, hawks and the Narukami banner came to mean loss.

The story is told in fragments, each ending with a dream she would never have again, then closes on a warm bathhouse day that may have been only a lazy nap after the rain.

Appearance: The in-game description calls it a bell lantern forged from purple jade. The text does not describe it further.

Lore: The item story opens on a half-asleep shrine maiden explaining to her companions that she was late because she dreamed of a bathhouse and thought she had already reached the meeting place. In truth, on the first day of the new year she had simply overslept. A frivolous young man teases her and a young woman of Seirai glares at him; an apprentice who is the oni's foster son says nothing. The text explains the Inazuman saying "First, bathhouses, second, hawks, third, Narukami": the sights of the first dream of the year, standing for health and longevity, high achievement and wishes fulfilled.

The story then moves through three losses. After a time of carefree years, bathhouse scenes never again appear in the maiden's dreams. In the second fragment a swordsman places his bow as a wager that he will return alive from the coming disaster; the text identifies this as the Thundering Pulse, and the maiden thinks him a hopeless gambler. The hawk of her dream, which she had taken as a sign that he would win, never returns either, leaving only drifting feathers. In the third, she dismisses omens as stories to fool children, a former friend having said that night's dreams reflect waking worries, until she dreams of the banner of Narukami rising over the sea like a storm of lightning. She laughs hollowly and, in the text's words, apologises to her master for squandering the art taught to her and for turning against the banner the master served, saying she cares nothing for her life or name so long as "he" lives on.

The final scene returns to the opening: the companion apologises for making light of the matter, and the maiden is urged not to stand daydreaming until the bathhouse closes. The text suggests that all the upheaval may have been a fleeting bathhouse dream and her awakening only a lazy nap after rain. The text never says how she regained a peaceful dream or whether the final scene is a dream, a memory or consolation. Read together with the Thundering Pulse text, the wiki's links identify the maiden as Asase Hibiki, the swordsman as Takamine the Mistsplitter, her master as Kitsune Saiguu, and the oni's foster son as Mikoshi Nagamasa. These identifications are the wiki's; the story itself leaves most of the figures unnamed.

Owners: No owner is named in the item text. The wiki notes only the dreaming maiden and her companions as the story's characters.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a five-star catalyst, base ATK 44, secondary stat Elemental Mastery 58. Passive "Bathhouses, Hawks, and Narukami": Elemental Mastery increases by 120-240 for 6s after triggering Swirl, by 96-192 for 9s after the wielder's Elemental Skill hits an opponent, and by 32-64 for 30s after the Elemental Burst hits an opponent, at refinement 1-5. It was the event-exclusive weapon of the Version 5.4 Epitome Invocation (2025-02-12), alongside Silvershower Heartstrings. The three effects echo the three dreams in the saying.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): it works as an object of wistful, gentle nostalgia, comfort offered by someone who has lost things. Keep the tone quiet; the story is sad but not melodramatic, and the maiden masks her feelings with indifference.

630.comment: Sunny Morning Sleep-In: First dreams of the year
630.content: The Inazuman saying in the item story lists the good omens of a first dream of the new year: bathhouses for health and longevity, hawks for high achievements, and Narukami for wishes fulfilled. In the story each fades from the shrine maiden's dreams as the Cataclysm approaches and arrives.

631.content:
Surf's Up (also: Aqua Remembrance, Scorching Summer): Surf's Up is a 5-star catalyst: a commemorative prize reserved for the champion of the First All-Tribe Surfing Championship, kept at the Leisurely Puffer while the tournament is being prepared.

Its story is a comic legend about the Pyro Archon Cochanina, a surfing champion, driving the Volcano Lord away from the People of the Springs.

Appearance: Canon gives no physical description of the item beyond calling it a commemorative piece. Keep descriptions simple and festive; do not add decorations.

Lore: A huge black Volcano Lord fouled the springs of the People of the Springs by dumping his filth into them. The Pyro Archon Cochanina, a surfing champion, left her famous blade at home, took only a surfboard, and tricked him out to sea.

She told him the tribe's treasure, the Iridescent Chalice left by the hero Uenuku, lay in the deep sea and that only he deserved it. When the clumsy Volcano Lord was dizzy, she tossed out a Drifting Pufferfish as the supposed key; he charged it, was struck, and fell off his board.

The Volcano Lord, a black and purple salamander-like monster, took advantage of other dragons' absence to occupy the Great Volcano of Tollan and ran roughshod over the people. He had been beaten many times by earlier Pyro Archons but always slipped away to hide at the volcano's bottom. This time he wanted to wash his filth in the springs, and the smoke he belched made the Flowcurrent Birds leave. The elder reported to Cochanina, who left her trusted weapon, the renowned Unu Pachacuti blade, and brought only a surfboard.

She flattered him into joining her, and he followed her wake behind the tribe's surfing champion. Struggling in the sea, he latched onto reeds and drifted a long time before reaching shore. Cochanina did not manage to expel him from Natlan, but he never again dared bother the People of the Springs.

The description's framing says the prize is in temporary storage at the Leisurely Puffer, with the shop owner (Mualani) as custodian, because the First All-Tribe Surfing Championship is only being prepared. The tale is also a window onto the Pyro Archons as surfers and tricksters: the wiki's profile of Cochanina adds that she was a kind, fun-loving mortal, known by the divine name Haborym, and later one of the Pyro Archons who contained the Bakunawa. Those later facts come from other quests, not from this item.

Owners: No wielder is named. Mualani is the custodian of the prize, not its holder.

Cochanina is the hero of the story but carried a surfboard and left her own blade at home; the tournament champion is the intended future owner. A scene giving it to a particular character is an invention.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star catalyst, base ATK 44 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.0.

Passive "Aqua Remembrance": Max HP is increased by 20% to 40%. Once every 15s, for 14s after using an Elemental Skill, the wielder gains 4 Scorching Summer stacks, each increasing Normal Attack DMG by 12% to 24%. During the effect every 1.5s a stack is lost after a Normal Attack hits, and a stack is gained (once per 1.5s) after triggering Vaporize on an opponent. Ascension uses the Blazing Sacrificial Heart materials, Will-series boss materials and Fang common materials.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: Natlanese locals tell the Volcano Lord story as a children's tale. The tone is playful; keep Cochanina clever and good-humoured, not solemn.

632.content: Aqua Remembrance is the passive of the catalyst Surf's Up (gameplay): a Max HP boost and Scorching Summer stacks that raise Normal Attack damage after an Elemental Skill and are refreshed by Vaporize.

633.content: The Volcano Lord is the villain of Surf's Up's story: a huge black-and-purple salamander-like monster who occupied the Great Volcano of Tollan and polluted the springs of the People of the Springs. Cochanina drove him back with a surfing race and a pufferfish, and he never again bothered that tribe.

634.content:
Sword of Descension: Sword of Descension is a 4-star sword in the game since Version 1.0 and given by mail to players who start on PS4 or PS5. Its description says it does not appear to belong to this world, and the item text calls it proof that the Traveler came to Teyvat by special means.

It can be wielded only by one who has challenged the "world", and it is addressed in second person to the Traveler as a weapon forged for one who challenges and pursues.

Appearance: A sword of unique craftsmanship. The wiki notes that the PlayStation triangle, circle, square and cross symbols appear on the handle, a real-world platform reference rather than an in-world detail.

Lore: The item text says only one who has challenged the "world" may wield such a sword, and that the Traveler wields it while searching for the answers hidden in this world.

It recalls the last time the sword was drawn: humankind tried to preserve a doomed world that was their last and only home, drawing steel against the law that all who exist must one day perish. Against the star-devouring darkness, the text says, the only fitting weapon is a sword, bearing the memory of those who faced their ends without fear.

In this world, the text adds, such a weapon can be used without trouble, not because the universe casts no shadows here nor because it suits the world's aesthetics, but because the search is perhaps why the Traveler descended to this realm. It ends by urging the wielder to take it, walk the earth and cut open the challenges and mysteries it offers.

The wiki links the "one who challenged the world" to the Descender motif and the darkness to the Abyss. Treat these as the wiki's cross-references to the item text's evocative framing rather than a plotted story: the text names neither the doomed world nor the sword's earlier wielders, so do not assign it to any specific character.

Owners: Addressed to the Traveler only. The text says only one who has challenged the "world" may wield it.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 39, ATK secondary stat, fixed at refinement 1 with one copy given. Its Descension passive is effective only on PlayStation: Normal and Charged Attack hits have a 50% chance to deal 200% ATK as DMG in a small area (once every 10s), and if the Traveler equips it their ATK rises by 66. Players on other platforms can obtain the weapon through cross-save, but the effect applies only when playing on PlayStation.

635.content:
Sword of Narzissenkreuz (also: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, Hero's Blade): The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is a 4-star sword received after the Rowboat's Wake quest in Fontaine. In the story it is the holy blade of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, its power faded when that story ended.

Its description calls it a sword that will now begin a new journey with the power remaining in it, commemorating a certain great dream. The Arkhe it carries, Pneuma or Ousia, can be switched at Annapausis.

Appearance: The only canon visuals are two forms, a Pneuma-aligned and an Ousia-aligned blade. The wiki gives no further description; avoid inventing engraving or hilt details.

Lore: A ceremonial sword of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. It was used in a ritual to separate mind from body and, in the Ordo's story, held reason itself.

Narzissenkreuz himself used it in that ritual, for example to grant a certain hilichurl intelligence, per the wiki lore summary. The quest-exclusive version, shown during Waking from the Great Dream, is described as a sacred blade with enough reason and will to create and destroy a universe, or a dream. After Rowboat's Wake it is replaced by the ordinary weapon.

The wiki reads the sword's makeup as based on ancient philosophies of the soul: the Ordo recreated Memory, Wish, Soul and Persona in the material world, each sealed in its Orthant, and their fusion is the reason that can cut or unite any will of water. Caterpillar says any object that holds reason can serve as the sword; Sandrone, on seeing the Traveler with it, calls it a savior's plaything. Narzissenkreuz's own closing line in the quest, as relayed by the wiki, is that the Holy Blade need not be a sword and could even be a gold-haired outlander.

The weapon description is a general passage about travellers: the sword in the hand and the dream in the heart as a traveller's trusted companions, and the eternal Traveler passing through many worlds and leaving a slightly brighter future. Its first paragraph repeats that of the Dull Blade. In the game's chain the blade is first the Holy Blade (Search in the Algae Sea), then the quest sword in Waking from the Great Dream, then this weapon in Rowboat's Wake.

Owners: Ann carries the blade in the story; the player receives the weapon at the end of the quest.

Narzissenkreuz is its original wielder. Sandrone's remark shows she knows the Traveler possesses it. Anyone else who sees it will not recognise it unless they know the Ordo.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 4-star sword, base ATK 42 at level 1, secondary stat ATK; obtained after Rowboat's Wake, version 4.2. Passive "Hero's Blade": for a wielder with no Arkhe of their own, Normal, Charged or Plunging Attacks that hit release a Pneuma or Ousia energy blast for a percentage of ATK, at most once every 12s. Refinement uses the material Surging Sacred Chalice, made from Drained Conch Cup at the Little Fountain.

How {{char}} behaves: Handle as a quest-end reward: someone who did not follow the Ordo's story will see only a plain, light blade. A character who knows Ann or Caterpillar may react with solemnity rather than treating it as a prize.

636.comment: Sword of Narzissenkreuz: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz
636.content: The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's ceremonial blade, used in a ritual separating mind from body and carried by Ann in the In the Wake of Narcissus quests. The player's weapon form (4-star) comes after the Rowboat's Wake quest.

637.content:
Symphonist of Scents (also: Seasoned Symphony): Symphonist of Scents is a 5-star polearm: an elegantly built baton said to have been wielded by a great musician, Euergetia, to bridge tune and taste.

Its story is a quiet one about the Remurian Harmost Euergetia and her use of authority to comfort homesick conquered people.

Appearance: Canon describes only an elegantly built polearm shaped like a conductor's baton. Arkhe-aligned wielders show a Pneuma or Ousia mark. Add nothing else.

Lore: During the long conquest of the tribes and kingdoms of the High Sea by the Legion Athanatoi, the Harmost Euergetia listened to the pleas of the conquered. The homesick people, though awed by the golden capital, missed the cuisines they had once enjoyed.

Stone golems need neither food nor drink, but the people were frail flesh and would grow dejected at poor fare. The God King's directives were the supreme rule, yet Euergetia reasoned that fulfilling a tiny wish was no offence in a symphony meant to embrace all living things. Her golden-haired colleague (the wiki links Boethius) grumbled behind her back but never stopped her.

She began an attunement in which hearing and taste could play in harmony: war drums and clashing swords could sing as one, and a melody with a simple meal could remind a slave of dishes they could only taste in memory, raising morale. The text admits it was mere illusory comfort, and asks whether illusions and dust are not the origin and end of all things.

Before emptying herself of desires, she had once been enchanted by gentle music and honey-sweet confections. Had she continued, the text says, even the uplifted ones might have enjoyed divine dishes and been anchored in a commonality. The golden empire never played the final notes: a veiled change overturned the fortress of white stone in a night, and both wicked and good plunged into the ocean depths. The simple wish to enjoy delicious food endured to present-day Fontaine. The wiki's Euergetia page adds that she died in the destruction of Remuria, that Boethius wished to revive Remuria with her but could not, and that she had a sweet tooth.

Owners: Euergetia, per the description (she is called the benefactrix on Remurian engravings).

Escoffier is paired with it at release only by convention (see uncertainties). Do not state that she holds the baton without a source.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not in-world): a 5-star polearm, base ATK 46 at level 1, secondary stat CRIT DMG; Weapon Event Wishes; introduced in Version 5.6. Passive "Seasoned Symphony": raises ATK, with an extra boost while the wielder is off-field; after the wielder initiates healing, they and those healed gain "Sweet Echoes" (ATK up for 3s), also while off-field. Values scale with refinement.

How {{char}} behaves: For scenes: the baton is an old tale of food and kindness; a chef or a Fontainian historian might know the story as a charming footnote. Keep the Remurians as conquerors, with the story's gentleness not erasing the slavery that frames it.

638.content: Euergetia was one of Remuria's four Harmosts, called the benefactrix. The weapon story of Symphonist of Scents shows her using her power to let conquered, homesick people taste their native dishes in their imaginations. She perished in Remuria's destruction.

639.content:
Tale of "Durin" (also: Tale of Durin, Durin's storybook, the book of Durin, Andersdotter's magic book): Tale of "Durin" is a quest item from the Draco Rubedo Chapter (6.2), Durin's Story Quest. It is a replica, made by the Hexenzirkel witch Alice, of the unfinished storybook left by Andersdotter ("M"), Durin's creator and mother. The original had to end up with Durin so he could write his own ending. The replica has no magical properties but keeps every twist of the story.

Alice gave the replica to the Traveler at the end of The Solution of Fate, saying that a witness to the tale deserves a keepsake. The player can use it to re-read all the storybook panels from The Magic Known as Storytelling; panels reflect the choices made during the quest.

Its in-game description stresses that the original magic book was meant to be handed over to Durin so that he could continue writing the story.

Lore: The original book was a joint work of the Hexenzirkel's witches, but Andersdotter died before finishing her part and left a great regret. She made sure Alice would give the book to Durin, whom she thought the only one who could resolve it. In the Story Quest the Traveler and Paimon help him fill the book's clues, entering the story world several times. The finale shows a simulated Simulanka-like world where Durin must break out of the story, and he receives his mother's pen and continues the tale. In post-quest dialogue Venti remarks that a line about Durin and Dvalin flying together over Mondstadt now describes a happy ending.

The quest runs over nine parts spanning at least five real days: a book in Starsand Shoal brings the Traveler into a story space; clues lead to the Mondstadt library (with Lisa), Venti, a game at Good Hunter and Stormterror's Lair, then to Sumeru City where the Wanderer helps. Albedo summons them to Dragonspine, where the witches' plan is explained: it needs Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic. Only the magic remained, and Alice supplies it by making the Traveler the reader and Durin the writer. In the story world the group can choose paths; the bad endings lead to fading characters, and Alice's recorded message lets them flip back pages. Each ending is written onto Durin, which is why she built that feature.

Outcome of the book. After Durin breaks free and takes up his mother's pen, Albedo finds his earlier symptoms gone, and Durin wears a freer outfit. Barbeloth, observing him, no longer sees his fate among the stars and evades his question, only telling him he was a lucky child. A fragment of Andersdotter's consciousness says farewell to Alice and delivers a letter to her child through a cinematic. Venti then sends Durin to fulfil a long-overdue wish, and Durin flies beside Dvalin and befriends him. As a reward Alice gives the Traveler the replica book.

Appearance: The in-game icon is a storybook; no further description is given in item text. The original was a magic book, and the quest depicts the story world with a Dodoco narrator.

Owners: Original: made by Hexenzirkel witches including Andersdotter, entrusted to Durin through Alice. Replica: Alice made it and gave it to the Traveler.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a quest item in the Traveler's possession. The story of the original book is complete; Durin continues writing his own story.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): the replica is a keepsake, not a magical object. Do not let it summon story worlds, alter fate or heal the Abyssal energy in Durin; those effects belonged to the original and Alice's magic. If Durin sees it he may be shy or touched, since the book is built from his mother's work.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a quest item obtained from The Solution of Fate that opens a gallery of the book's panels reflecting the player's choices.

640.comment: Tale of "Durin": The Solution of Fate
640.content: In The Solution of Fate, the finale of Durin's Story Quest, the book pulls the group into a story world in which Durin must defy the fate of the original dragon. His mother appears as a manifestation, hands him her pen so he can keep writing, and he wins his own ending. Alice then gives the Traveler a replica of the book.

641.comment: Tale of "Durin": Alice and the replica
641.content: Alice tells the Traveler the copy is not magical in the same way as the original, but every twist and turn remains. Earlier, in a recorded message, she explains that she built a special feature into the original so the Traveler and Paimon, the witnesses, could turn back the pages after a bad ending.

642.content:
Tales Carried by the Northwind (also: Tales Carried by the Northwind (book)): It reads as a memorial anthology. Its fragments are elegies and heroic verse about leaders who held the title of Starshyna, and about the cost of leadership to those who followed them.

Appearance: A 3-star one-volume book collection, found on a box near Kofitse in Piramida.

Lore: Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov: one poem. An old man with a weapon stands against towering black waves while a voice in the mist reproaches him for the deaths of young men who trusted him, the orphans he adopted, the unsent distress signal and the fallen Lighthouse. He turns to the ocean and polishes his axe once more.

The anthology is incomplete by design: the excerpts are numbered III, VI and VIII, with ellipses where material is missing. They belong to different voices. Solovei's work mixes personal regret with a call to keep a beacon alight, and Mayakov's poem presents a leader's self-reproach after a disaster.

The Solovei excerpts are numbered VI and VIII and the Mayakov poem III, so the numbering does not run in order of the surviving text. Poem VIII ends by naming the generations that inherited the Starshyna name, and the Mayakov poem is the only fragment that mentions adopted orphans. The book gives no dates for any of the poems.

Owners: No owner; it is a loose book in Piramida.

Gameplay: Gameplay note (not in-world): a 3-star Book Collection added in 6.3, found near Kofitse in Piramida.

643.comment: Tales Carried by the Northwind: Starshyna Verse
643.content: The book collects verse about Starshynas, attributed to Silvestr Petrovich Solovei and Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov. It is damaged and fragmentary, so any claim about the people or events behind the poems should be framed as what the verse says rather than as established history.

644.content:
Tamayuratei no Ohanashi (also: Tamayuratei, the lantern youkai's polearm): Tamayuratei no Ohanashi is a four-star polearm of the Youkai series, obtained during the Version 5.4 event Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival. Its text tells of an invisible youkai who took the form of a spectral flame, stole stories at hearths and braziers and retold them at banquets of wandering spirits, and was named "Tamayuratei" by the kitsune chief Hakushin. After the Cataclysm it became a messenger of battle reports and wore itself away.

Appearance: The weapon is a lantern-topped polearm. The wiki notes that its lantern has dynamic night-time lighting when effects are set high (a client detail, not lore); the item text does not describe its look.

Lore: The text begins with spectral flames drifting through the wilds and an invisible, secret-loving youkai taking the form of such a flame, flitting from hearth to brazier to steal stories from people chatting over tea. It retold them at banquets of wandering spirits, for amusing the great while they drank was the purpose of the Otogishu. At one such evening Hakushin, chief of the kitsune, sighed that she wished time could stop, and raised her sake cup to give the lowly youkai on stage the title "Tamayuratei".

Her melancholy proved prophetic, since the Cataclysm's dark, corrosive tide engulfed the land and the hundred-youkai revels gave way to weeping. Remembering the great one who named it, the frail youkai threw itself into the war, darting from fire to fire and turning its eloquence to the precise relaying of battle reports and enemy movements. The constant effort took a toll: it divided its essence again and again, nearly exhausting its spirit, could no longer speak from within its lantern, and lost even its cherished memories.

The closing legend is a gentle one: the bewildered youkai has forgotten everything and now appears only at the liveliest occasions, when crowds gather to hear fantastic tales, and perhaps the storytellers' atmosphere lets it recall, briefly, a past it cannot reclaim. This is event-sourced text (the weapon is only obtainable during the Mikawa festival event), so it should be treated as folklore told within Inazuma rather than universally known history.

Owners: No human owner is named; the story is about an unnamed youkai who bears the title "Tamayuratei".

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): four-star polearm of the Youkai series. Base ATK 44, secondary stat Energy Recharge 6.7%. Passive "Busybody's Running Light" raises ATK and Movement SPD by 10% for 10s after using an Elemental Skill. Obtained in the 5.4 event "Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival".

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay use (this project's suggestion, not canon text): a storyteller's lantern: good for scenes about gossip, festival evenings and forgotten loyalty.

645.comment: Tamayuratei no Ohanashi: Hakushin's naming of the youkai
645.content: In the Tamayuratei no Ohanashi text, Hakushin, chief of the kitsune, raises a sake cup at a banquet of spirits and gives the title "Tamayuratei" to a lowly lantern youkai, wishing aloud that time could stop. The event-sourced story says the youkai later devoted itself to the Cataclysm's war effort in her memory.

646.content:
Tenacity of the Millelith (also: Flower of Accolades, Ceremonial War-Plume, Orichalceous Time-Dial, Noble's Pledging Vessel, General's Ancient Helm): Tenacity of the Millelith is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Liyue's soldiers. Its five pieces are a golden flower, a falcon-feather plume, a sun-and-moon time-dial, a golden oath cup and a general's helmet, and their item text commemorates the Millelith who held the Chasm against the Abyss alongside a nameless yaksha, dying there so civilians could escape.

Added in version 1.5. The text is Liyue folk memory about an event 500 years before the present, in the time of the Cataclysm. Rex Lapis is said to have sent the Millelith to defend the Chasm mines when the Abyss flooded in; the soldiers who stayed to cover the retreat are remembered in the Millelith's ceremonial dress.

Appearance: Ceremonial military gear of Liyue: a flower made of gold leaf, a plume from a high-altitude bird of prey worn on parade, a bronze time-dial powered by sunlight and moonlight, a golden cup used to swear oaths, and a splendid ancient helmet which looks new again once the dust is cleaned away.

Lore: Rex Lapis is said to have ordered the Millelith to defend the Chasm mines when the Abyss flooded in. Fighting beside a nameless yaksha, a rearguard stayed behind to cover the civilians' escape and fell there; Millelith ceremonial dress (golden flower, feather plume) honours them.

Each piece adds an element. A meteorite fell into the Chasm, turning the ground to Glazed Sand Crystal; later, when the Abyss flooded out, Rex Lapis ordered the Millelith to defend the mines (Flower of Accolades). The Millelith take their feather ornaments from the yaksha, whose plumage was torn in battle and whose fallen feathers became a symbol of hope (Ceremonial War-Plume). Because fighting beside the yaksha exposed mortals to karma and the darkness of killing, soldiers kept a fixed marching rhythm with a time-dial, one squad taking the field as another withdrew (Orichalceous Time-Dial). The Millelith's first elders swore loyalty to Rex Lapis over a golden cup before marching into the abyss (Noble's Pledging Vessel). The front-line troops under a commander in helmets charged so the afflicted civilians could flee, and when the gloom cleared the yaksha had vanished and the soldiers lay at rest (General's Ancient Helm).
The set treats memory as its theme: the names of mortals and adepti alike are said to have been forgotten, yet their deeds are not. Today's Liyue Harbor is described as still peaceful because the Cataclysm was quelled, and soldiers wear the golden flower in honour of their forebears. The text also records two later episodes: a conceited adventurer who, centuries after, recovered the pledging cup from the Chasm and found it untarnished, and a miner who found a time-dial a hundred years after the battle.

The pieces include a deliberate ambiguity about the yaksha. Ceremonial War-Plume reports that people claim the yaksha was not acting under Rex Lapis's command but paying for an old sin of cowardice and neglected duty, and that Rex Lapis, moved by the sacrifice, kept a long silence; General's Ancient Helm, by contrast, says the yaksha fought at Rex Lapis's order. The text neither resolves this nor says what happened to the yaksha afterwards, only that it is thought to have returned to a free life among the clouds. Orichalceous Time-Dial adds an urban legend of a black-robed collector of curios who bought up every time-dial at a generous price and deflected all questions; the wiki connects him to Zhongli, but the text itself says only that time may eventually explain his reasons. Together, the pieces give a mortal-centred picture of the Cataclysm in Liyue: the heroes are a rearguard nobody remembers by name.

Owners: No owner is named. The text speaks of Millelith soldiers, their commander and a nameless yaksha; the wiki links the yaksha to Bosacius.

Gameplay: Game mechanics (not lore): obtained from the Ridge Watch domain and the Artifact Strongbox. 2-piece: HP +20%. 4-piece: when an Elemental Skill hits an opponent, all nearby party members gain ATK +20% and Shield Strength +30% for 3s, triggerable once per 0.5s, including while the wearer is off-field.

647.comment: Tenacity of the Millelith: Tenacity of the Millelith
647.content: Artifact set whose item text honours the Millelith soldiers and a nameless yaksha who died defending the Chasm mines from the Abyss at the time of the Cataclysm, about 500 years ago.

648.comment: Tenacity of the Millelith: The Chasm stand (item-text account)
648.content: In the folk account of the Tenacity of the Millelith set, a meteorite crater in the Chasm turned the ground to Glazed Sand Crystal. When the Abyss flooded in, Rex Lapis sent the Millelith to defend the mines; the troops escorted civilians out, and a rearguard stayed with a nameless yaksha and fell in the Chasm. The Abyss receded, the glaze sands shone again, and the yaksha vanished. Treat the details as legend: the text is partly contradictory about whether the yaksha acted on Rex Lapis's orders.

649.comment: Tenacity of the Millelith: Millelith ceremonial plume and golden flower
649.content: The set explains Millelith ceremonial dress: the golden flower honours the dead of the Chasm, and the feather plume worn on ceremonial occasions is said to have been inspired by the yaksha's torn plumage. The plumes raise civilian morale and awe foreign visitors.

650.content:
Teyvat Travel Guide (also: Teyvat Geographic Special Edition, Alice's Mondstadt Diaries, Alice's Travels in Liyue, Alice's Inazuma Diaries): The Teyvat Travel Guide is a three-volume magazine series from the Adventurers' Guild. Under the heading 'Teyvat Geographic Special Edition', each issue is a short travel diary by Alice, covering Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma. Alice is a cheerful experimenter and the diaries treat sightseeing as an excuse for explosives, potions and mischief.

The descriptions say each issue introduces great sceneries across Teyvat. Vol. 3 first became available in the limited-time Hues of the Violet Garden event (2.6), and Kuroda continues to sell it afterwards.

Appearance: Glossy magazine issues whose cover reads 'Travel Guide' in the Teyvat script. Entries are headed by place names and written in the first person in a breezy, boastful, sometimes self-deprecating voice.

Lore: Vol. 1 (Mondstadt) visits Dadaupa Gorge, Starsnatch Cliff, Windrise, Falcon Coast, the Whispering Woods, Brightcrown Canyon and Stormterror's Lair. Vol. 2 (Liyue) visits Dihua Marsh and Wangshu Inn, Guili Plains, Jueyun Karst, Yaoguang Shoal and Guyun Stone Forest. Vol. 3 (Inazuma) visits Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine, Inazuma City, Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island.

- Vol. 1: Alice proposes absurd energy schemes for the hilichurls of Dadaupa Gorge and for demolishing Starsnatch Cliff; Lisa answers with silence and Kaeya rejects her plan. She tries to launch hilichurls from the oak at Windrise (Vennessa is said to have ascended there), and Jean has an Outrider (Amber) assigned to watch her at Falcon Coast. She tries to control a Ruin Guard in Brightcrown Canyon with a hilichurl, with gruesome results, and comments on Decarabian's ring-shaped city.
- Vol. 2: at Wangshu Inn she notes a silent lodger on the top floor and enjoys the kitchen for alchemy practice. At the Guili Plains checkpoint she cured a guard's stutter with a potion whose side effect makes him imitate everyone. At Jueyun Karst she muses on adepti visions and mushrooms, her travel companion Zhongli laughs at her theory about the stone pillars, and at Yaoguang Shoal she loses shells and a prototype seashell-boat. At Guyun Stone Forest she wonders about the Geo Archon's victory over the sea monster and the unstable ley lines.
- Vol. 3: at the Grand Narukami Shrine she mentions Yae Miko, who out-drank her. In Inazuma City she meets Naganohara Ryuunosuke and Yoimiya and is sent off by the fire brigade; she mentions Klee's Golden Apple Archipelago, an accident in the Imperial Kitchen that hurt Kujou Sara, Tenshukaku's guards, and Kamisato Ayaka declining her idol group invitation. At Tatarasuna she meets Kagami Gozen and boasts of modifying the Mikage Furnace. At Yashiori Island she admires the Shogun's wards and mentions Washizu of Higi Village, Nazuchi Beach pirates and Asase Shrine.

- The diaries repeat Alice's habits across nations: building weapons from gadgets, testing potions on bystanders, and being watched by officials (the Knights of Favonius in Mondstadt and soldiers sent from Tenshukaku in Inazuma).
- Her remarks about Mondstadt's and Liyue's gods (the Anemo Archon is 'undisciplined', the Geo Archon's strike a possible joke) are her opinions, not confirmed lore.
- The Inazuma volume contains lines that can be read as speaking about the Raiden Shogun and Yae Miko with long acquaintance; note that they come from Alice's narration.
- The Vol. 3 remarks on Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island give an outsider's view of the Tatarigami curse and the miners' chronic illness despite the Shogun's wards.
- The diary mentions a possible coming war in Inazuma and astrologers' predictions; treat that as Alice's wry aside from the time of writing, not a date.
- Where Alice's diary and the places' own entries disagree, prefer the place entries.

Owners: No individual owner. Alice is the diarist; Lisa gives Vol. 1, Chang the Ninth gives Vol. 2, and Kuroda (and, for a time, Murata) sells Vol. 3.

Gameplay: Game note: a three-volume collectible book collection. Vol. 1 comes from Lisa's quest Lost Book, Vol. 2 from Chang the Ninth's quest Justice Is Its Own Reward, and Vol. 3 from the limited-time Hues of the Violet Garden event (2.6) and Kuroda's shop afterwards. No stats.

651.comment: Teyvat Travel Guide: Alice's Mondstadt Diaries
651.content: Vol. 1 records Alice's visits to Dadaupa Gorge, Starsnatch Cliff, Windrise, Falcon Coast, the Whispering Woods, Brightcrown Canyon and Stormterror's Lair, with several explosive proposals that Kaeya, Jean's Outrider and Lisa tactfully decline.

652.comment: Teyvat Travel Guide: Alice's Travels in Liyue
652.content: Vol. 2 records Alice at Dihua Marsh, Wangshu Inn, the Guili Plains, Jueyun Karst, Yaoguang Shoal and Guyun Stone Forest, with her companion Zhongli, a potion that left a checkpoint guard imitating everyone, and a boat prototype that exploded.

653.comment: Teyvat Travel Guide: Alice's Inazuma Diaries
653.content: Vol. 3 was first obtained during the Hues of the Violet Garden event in 2.6 and is later sold by Kuroda. It records Mt. Yougou, Inazuma City, Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island, including Alice's meetings with Yae Miko, Naganohara Ryuunosuke, Yoimiya, Kagami Gozen and Washizu.

654.content:
The Alley Flash (also: Alley Flash): The Alley Flash is a four-star sword of the Alley series: a straight, night-black longsword once carried by a thief who roamed Mondstadt's benighted streets. The item text tells of a young noble who stole it from his family's vault and used it, never staining it with blood, to rob the rich for the poor.

Appearance: Item text calls it a mighty, noble longsword as black as night, its darkened blade blending into nights when people feared lighting fires. It is said many later knightly swords, such as the Favonius Sword, were modelled on this design. A bard's song says it was blackened during the age of the aristocracy.

Lore: The young noble (identified by the wiki as Parsifal) read the tales and songs of his upright ancestors, which sowed rebellion in him. He left his venerable house, stole the sword, and hid in the streets, living among common folk in alleys and taverns and using his noble swordsmanship to rob the rich for the poor. The edge was never marred by blood, nor was the thief's heart.

As wine, song and youth faded and events passed, he buried his beloved blade under moonlight and fled across the sea. He remembered the night he took it from his family's vault, and the vow he made to his family, past and present, to his land and to Eberhart: to use his strength, even if only a little, to turn the dark world around.

Related items fill in the legend: the Wine and Song songbook sings of the same gentleman thief, and the Alley Hunter is the black bow he carried. Eberhart is called a sworn brother in English and a half-brother in the Chinese original. The sword is thus a symbol of rebellion from within the aristocracy rather than from outside it.

Owners: Item text refers to a young noble turned thief; the wiki identifies him as Parsifal. He took it from his house's vault and buried it before leaving.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Alley-series four-star sword, base ATK 45, Elemental Mastery 12 secondary, passive 'Itinerant Hero'. Released in Version 1.4 via Weapon Event Wishes.

655.content:
The Bell (also: Bell greatsword, clock greatsword): The Bell is a four-star claymore of the Wanderer's Troupe series. It is a heavy greatsword with a clock set into it, whose internal mechanisms are long damaged. Its story belongs to Kreuzlied, a former Lawrence clan noble turned traitor who travelled with the Troupe.

Appearance: Item text describes a strange greatsword decorated with an exquisite clock. After the Troupe disbanded it was soaked in acid, which rusted the gears; it is still a lethal weapon. Its clockwork once gave the wielder and friends a combat rhythm.

Lore: Kreuzlied once belonged to the ruling Lawrence clan but became a traitor and outcast and travelled with the Wanderer's Troupe. In that era scholars and bards ignored history because the aristocracy preferred wilful ignorance of their own decay to history's judgement, yet they trembled at the sound of this blade, the toll of the bell of judgment.

What punishment Kreuzlied suffered after the failed uprising was never made public, which the text takes as proof of his privilege. Legend says that after being dismissed from office he founded a secret society to bring down the aristocracy, and gave his full help to the enslaved gladiator Vennessa when she revolted.

A once-popular rumour held that the society kept working behind the scenes to help the Knights of Favonius protect Mondstadt through deeds no knight should take part in, and that the Wolf Pup Rostam secretly ran it behind the Grand Master Arundolyn's back. The text presents this only as rumour, so do not state it as fact.

Owners: Kreuzlied, who travelled with the Troupe.

Freminet is shown wielding the ascended version in his official art and in the Version 4.6 trailer, and the base version in the Into the Sunlight story; that is presentation, not a canon ownership claim.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: Wanderer's Troupe-series four-star claymore, base ATK 42, HP 9% secondary, passive 'Rebellious Guardian' (a shield; damage rises while any shield protects the wearer). Available in the standard Wanderlust Invocation and event wishes.

656.content:
The Black Sword (also: Black Sword): The Black Sword is a 4-star sword from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn, in the game since Version 1.0. The in-game short description calls it a pitch-black longsword that thirsts for violence and conflict. The full text is the parable of a bright white knight whose pursuit of justice slid into slaughter.

Its text ties to the Bloodstained Chivalry artifact set, and the wiki notes that the decoration atop the blade resembles that set's circlet.

Appearance: A pitch-black longsword with a decoration on top of the blade. The wiki notes the decoration strongly resembles the circlet of the Bloodstained Chivalry artifact set. In the story the knight's sword once hung at his hip with a mirror sheen before the bloodshed blackened it.

Lore: A blade that thirsts after fresh blood is awakened by its scent, and those who wield and nourish it keep killing until even a pure soul is blackened. The text tells of a white knight who rode to cut down injustice, beasts and fires, taught by the Wolf Pup in chivalry, justice and swordsmanship.

The knight recalls losing himself in cutting, slashing and piercing, feeling a tingle at the blade's meeting flesh and believing this was justice getting its due. A voice calls him a fool and says slaughter in the name of justice is still slaughter; he answers that it is justice.

The narration urges him to go on though the white flowers the maidens give him are bloodied black, though his sword no longer gleams, his face turns hideous and he must wear an iron mask, and though those he defends do not understand him. The black-stained knight persists, pursuing monsters in the name of justice.

The text ends with him coming upon an ancient, ruined realm where he found the ultimate injustice, leaving the reader to supply what that was. The wiki links the realm to Khaenri'ah, the injustice to hilichurls, the knight to Roland and the Wolf Pup to Rostam, and the maidens' flowers and the iron mask to the Bloodstained Chivalry set's items. Treat these links as the wiki's cross-references.

Owners: The item text names no owner. The wiki links the white knight to Roland; see his entry for the details.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): 4-star sword, base ATK 42, CRIT Rate secondary stat. Passive Justice: Normal and Charged Attack DMG rises 20 to 40 per cent by refinement, and a CRIT hit from those attacks restores 60 to 100 per cent of ATK as HP, at most once every 5s. The healing can trigger even if the hit deals no damage to an invulnerable or shielded enemy. Obtained through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn bundle.

657.comment: The Black Sword: The White Knight
657.content: The white knight of The Black Sword's text rode to cut down injustice and was taught by the Wolf Pup, but his zeal for justice turned into killing, blackening his sword and face until he wore an iron mask. The wiki links him to Roland. See Roland's and the Bloodstained Chivalry entries.

658.content:
